name: Adobong Manok
steps: Pat the chicken dry and season with salt and pepper. Heat cooking oil in a pot and brown the chicken pieces on both sides, then set aside.
In the same pot, sauté the onion and garlic until soft. Return the chicken along with the bay leaf and black pepper.
Pour in the soy sauce and enough water to half-cover the chicken. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer, covered, for 20 minutes.
Add the vinegar and let it simmer uncovered for a few minutes without stirring, so the sharp smell cooks off, then stir it in.
Add the potato, cut into chunks, and simmer until the chicken is tender and the potato is cooked through, about 15 more minutes.
Uncover and simmer until the sauce reduces to a thick coating. Chicken is done at 74°C (165°F) at the thickest part. Serve hot.

name: Adobong Baboy
steps: Cut the pork belly into cubes and season with salt and black pepper.
Heat cooking oil in a pot and brown the pork on all sides. Add the onion and garlic and cook until fragrant.
Pour in the soy sauce, vinegar and bay leaf. Bring to a boil, then simmer uncovered a few minutes before stirring, so the vinegar loses its raw edge.
Cover, lower the heat, and simmer until the pork is fork-tender, about 45 minutes, adding a splash of water if the pot runs dry.
Uncover and simmer until the sauce reduces and coats the pork. Pork is safe at 63°C (145°F) with a short rest, but for adobo cook until it falls apart.
Skim off excess fat if the sauce looks oily, then serve.

name: Adobo sa Gata
steps: Cut the pork shoulder into cubes and season with salt.
Heat cooking oil, brown the pork, and set aside. Sauté the onion and garlic in the same pot.
Return the pork, add the soy sauce, vinegar, bay leaf and black pepper. Bring to a boil and simmer uncovered a few minutes before stirring.
Cover and simmer until the pork is almost tender, about 30 minutes.
Pour in the coconut milk and whole bird's eye chilies. Simmer uncovered, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens and the oil starts to separate.
Cook until the pork is tender with no pink at the center and the sauce clings to it. Serve hot.

name: Adobong Kambing
steps: Rinse the goat meat. Some cooks blanch it in boiling water for a few minutes first and discard that water, which softens the strong smell; drain well.
Heat cooking oil, sauté the onion and garlic, then add the goat and cook until it changes color.
Add the soy sauce, vinegar, bay leaf, black pepper and whole bird's eye chilies. Bring to a boil, then simmer uncovered a few minutes before stirring.
Cover and simmer over low heat until the goat is tender, 45–60 minutes, topping up water as needed.
Uncover and reduce the sauce until it thickens and clings to the meat.
Goat should reach at least 63°C (145°F); simmering until fork-tender takes it well past that. Serve hot.

name: Kalderetang Baka
steps: Cut the beef into cubes and season with salt. Heat cooking oil and brown the beef in batches, then set aside.
In the same pot, sauté the garlic and onion. Return the beef, add the bay leaf and beef broth. Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer until the beef is nearly tender, about 1 hour.
Stir in the soy sauce and tomato sauce and simmer uncovered another 10 minutes.
Add the potato and carrot, cut into chunks, and cook until they begin to soften.
Stir in the liver spread until the sauce turns thick and glossy, then add the red and green bell pepper, green olives and chili flakes.
Simmer until the beef is fork-tender and the vegetables are cooked, then adjust salt. Beef should show no pink at the center.

name: Kalderetang Kambing
steps: Marinate the goat meat in the vinegar, pineapple juice and salt for at least 30 minutes; this also tames the gamey smell.
Heat cooking oil and brown the marinated goat, reserving the marinade, then sauté the onion and garlic in the same pot.
Return the goat, pour in the reserved marinade plus enough water to cover, and simmer covered until nearly tender, 45–60 minutes.
Stir in the tomato sauce and whole bird's eye chilies. Add the potato and carrot, cut into chunks, and simmer until they soften.
Stir in the liver spread until the sauce thickens, then add the red and green bell pepper, pickle relish and green olives.
Simmer until the goat is fork-tender and the sauce clings to it. Season with salt and pepper.

name: Kalderetang Manok
steps: Season the chicken with black pepper. Heat cooking oil and brown the chicken pieces, then set aside.
Sauté the onion and garlic, add the chopped tomato and cook until it breaks down.
Return the chicken, add the tomato sauce and a chicken cube dissolved in water to cover. Bring to a boil, cover and simmer until the chicken is nearly tender.
Add the potato and carrot, cut into chunks, and cook until they soften.
Stir in the liver spread until the sauce thickens, then add the green bell pepper.
Simmer until the chicken reaches 74°C (165°F) and the vegetables are tender. Stir in grated cheese until melted, then serve.

name: Mechado
steps: Cut the beef into strips or cubes and marinate briefly with the soy sauce and calamansi juice.
Render the pork fat in a pot over medium heat with a little cooking oil until it releases its fat, then discard the solid bits.
Brown the marinated beef in the rendered fat, then set aside. Sauté the onion and garlic.
Return the beef, add the bay leaf, tomato sauce and enough water to cover. Simmer covered until the beef is tender, about 1 hour.
Add the potato and carrot, cut into chunks, and simmer until tender.
Add the green and red bell pepper, season with salt and pepper, and simmer a few more minutes. Beef should be fully cooked through.

name: Afritadang Manok
steps: Season the chicken with salt and pepper. Heat cooking oil and brown the chicken pieces, then set aside.
Sauté the onion and garlic, add the chopped tomato and cook until softened.
Return the chicken, season with fish sauce, and add enough water to half-cover. Bring to a boil, cover and simmer until nearly tender.
Add the potato and carrot, cut into chunks, and simmer until they begin to soften.
Add the red and green bell pepper and green peas, then simmer until the chicken reaches 74°C (165°F) and the vegetables are tender.
Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper and serve.

name: Afritadang Baboy
steps: Cut the pork belly into cubes and season with salt and pepper. Heat cooking oil and brown the pork, then set aside.
Sauté the onion and garlic, then return the pork.
Stir in the tomato sauce, tomato paste and fish sauce, then add enough water to cover. Bring to a boil, cover and simmer until the pork is nearly tender, about 40 minutes.
Add the potato and carrot, cut into chunks, and simmer until they soften.
Add the green and red bell pepper and simmer a few more minutes.
Cook until the pork is tender with no pink remaining, then adjust salt and pepper and serve.

name: Menudo
steps: Cut the pork shoulder into small cubes and cut the beef liver into similar-sized pieces, keeping them separate.
Heat cooking oil with the annatto seeds until the oil turns red-orange, then remove the seeds. Sauté the onion and garlic in the annatto oil.
Add the pork and cook until it browns, then add the chopped tomato and cook until it softens.
Season with fish sauce, add enough water to cover, and simmer covered until the pork is nearly tender.
Add the potato and carrot, cut into cubes, along with the chickpeas and raisins, and simmer until they soften.
Stir in the beef liver and the green and red bell pepper; liver cooks quickly, so simmer just until it firms up and the sauce thickens, about 5 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper. Pork should show no pink; take care not to overcook the liver, which turns tough and chalky.

name: Pochero
steps: Cut the pork belly into serving pieces and season with black pepper. Heat cooking oil, brown the pork, then set aside.
Sauté the onion, garlic and chopped tomato until softened. Return the pork, add the tomato sauce and enough water to cover.
Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer until the pork is nearly tender, about 45 minutes.
Add the potato, cut into chunks, and the chickpeas, and simmer until the potato softens.
Add the banana, cut into chunks, and the string beans, and simmer a few minutes.
Add the cabbage and bok choy last, and simmer just until wilted, about 3 minutes, so they stay bright.
Season with fish sauce and black pepper. Pork should be cooked through with no pink remaining.

name: Bistek Tagalog
steps: Slice the beef thinly. Marinate it with the soy sauce, lemon juice, crushed garlic and black pepper for at least 15 minutes.
Slice one onion into rings and set aside for the topping.
Heat cooking oil in a pan and sear the onion rings briefly until just softened, then remove and set aside.
In the same pan, sauté more garlic and onion, then add the beef, reserving the marinade, and sear over high heat until browned but not overcooked.
Pour in the reserved marinade and a little water, and simmer briefly until the sauce reduces slightly.
Season with salt and black pepper. Plate the beef with the sauce and top with the seared onion rings.

name: Dinuguan
steps: Simmer the pork belly in water with the ginger until just tender, then drain and cut into bite-sized cubes; keep it separate from the chopped pork.
Heat cooking oil and sauté the onion and garlic until fragrant. Add the chopped pork and pork belly and cook until lightly browned.
Pour in the pork blood, stirring constantly so it doesn't clump, and bring to a gentle simmer; it thickens and darkens the sauce as it cooks.
Add the vinegar and let it simmer uncovered a few minutes without stirring, so the sharp smell cooks off, then stir it in along with the long green chili.
Season with fish sauce and brown sugar, and simmer until the sauce is thick and the pork is fully cooked through, with no pink remaining.
Keep the pot at a gentle simmer until the blood sauce reaches 74°C (165°F) and is fully set, not runny or bright red. Season with salt and pepper and serve.

name: Sisig
steps: Place the pig ears, pig snout and pork belly in a pot with the bay leaf, ginger and salt. Cover with water and boil until tender, 45 minutes to an hour.
Drain and let cool, then chop the meat and ears into small bits.
Heat a pan (a sizzling plate if you have one) and sear the chopped meat until browned and slightly crisp at the edges.
Add the finely chopped onion and cook briefly until softened.
Stir in the liver spread and a splash of vinegar, and season with salt, sugar and black pepper.
Off the heat, stir in a spoonful of mayonnaise and a squeeze of lime juice, then finish with a dash of liquid seasoning. Pork should be fully cooked through with no pink remaining.

name: Lechon Kawali
steps: Place the pork belly in a pot with the bay leaf, salt and enough water to cover. Boil until the meat is tender but the skin is still intact, about 45 minutes.
Drain the pork well and pat it completely dry; a dry skin is what makes it crackle. Let it air-dry, uncovered, for at least 30 minutes.
Season the dried pork with salt and black pepper.
Heat cooking oil in a deep pot until hot. Carefully lower in the pork and fry until the skin blisters and turns golden and crisp, turning as needed.
Drain on a rack. The pork is already fully cooked from boiling, so frying is only to crisp the skin; check that no pink remains before serving.
Chop into serving pieces once the skin has cooled and crisped.

name: Crispy Pata
steps: Place the pork hock in a pot with the garlic, bay leaf, salt, black pepper and enough water and lemon-lime soda to cover. Boil until the meat is tender, about 1 to 1.5 hours.
Drain and pat the hock completely dry, then let it air-dry uncovered for at least 30 minutes so the skin crisps well when fried.
Heat plenty of cooking oil in a deep pot. Carefully lower in the hock and fry, turning occasionally, until the skin is deep golden and crackling.
While it fries, mix a dipping sauce of vinegar, soy sauce, chopped shallots, garlic and sliced bird's eye chili, seasoned with salt and pepper.
Drain the fried hock on a rack and let it rest briefly before chopping. The meat is already cooked through from boiling; frying only crisps the skin.
Serve hot with the dipping sauce on the side.

name: Humba
steps: Cut the pork belly into chunks. Heat cooking oil and brown the pork, then set aside.
Sauté the onion and garlic. Return the pork, add the soy sauce, vinegar, bay leaf and black pepper. Bring to a boil, then simmer uncovered a few minutes before stirring.
Pour in the pineapple juice, add the salted black beans and brown sugar, and cover. Simmer over low heat until the pork is very tender, about 1 hour.
Add the canned pineapple chunks and sliced banana heart, and simmer another 10 minutes.
Uncover and reduce the sauce until thick and sticky, coating the pork.
Season with salt to taste. Pork should be fully cooked and falling-apart tender.

name: Hamonado
steps: Cut the pork belly into chunks and season with salt and black pepper.
Heat cooking oil, brown the pork, then set aside. Sauté the garlic until fragrant.
Return the pork, add the soy sauce, pineapple juice and brown sugar. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer until tender, about 45 minutes.
Add the canned pineapple chunks and simmer another 10 minutes.
Uncover and simmer until the sauce reduces to a sticky glaze coating the pork.
Pork should be fully cooked with no pink remaining. Serve hot.

name: Beef Tapa
steps: Slice the carabao meat thinly, against the grain.
Marinate the slices with the fish sauce, brown sugar, crushed garlic and black pepper for at least 30 minutes, or overnight for deeper flavor.
Heat cooking oil in a pan over medium-high heat.
Fry the marinated meat in batches, without crowding the pan, until browned and cooked through, a few minutes per side.
The slices are thin, so check that no pink remains at the center before removing from the heat.
Serve hot, with the pan juices spooned over.

name: Tocino
steps: Slice the pork shoulder thinly.
Mix the brown sugar, garlic powder, salt, black pepper, a few drops of food coloring and pineapple juice into a marinade.
Toss the pork slices in the marinade, coating each piece, and refrigerate for at least 8 hours or overnight.
Heat cooking oil in a pan over medium heat. Cook the marinated pork with a splash of water, letting the liquid reduce as the pork cooks through.
Once the liquid has mostly evaporated, let the brown sugar caramelize on the surface, turning to brown evenly.
Cook until no pink remains in the center. Serve hot.

name: Longganisa
steps: In a bowl, mix the ground pork with the pork fat, minced garlic, soy sauce, anise wine, vinegar, brown sugar, salt, black pepper and paprika until well combined.
Cover and refrigerate the mixture for at least a few hours, or overnight, so the flavors set.
Stuff the mixture into the hog casings, twisting at intervals to form links (or shape into small logs if skipping the casings).
Heat cooking oil in a pan over medium heat. Cook the sausages with a splash of water, turning occasionally, until the water evaporates.
Continue cooking in the rendered fat until the sausages are browned on all sides and the center reaches 71°C (160°F).
Cut one open to confirm no pink remains at the center before serving.

name: Embutido
steps: In a large bowl, mix the ground pork with the breadcrumbs, a raw egg, tomato sauce, chopped onion, carrot, red and green bell pepper, pickle relish and raisins. Season with salt and pepper.
Divide the mixture in half. Lay each half on a sheet of foil and shape into a log, placing sliced hard-boiled egg and vienna sausage down the center along with a strip of cheese.
Roll tightly into a log and wrap securely in the foil, twisting the ends closed.
Steam the wrapped logs over simmering water for about 45 minutes to an hour, until firm.
Remove from the steamer and let cool slightly before unwrapping. Check that the center reaches at least 71°C (160°F), the safe minimum for ground pork, with no pink remaining.
Slice and serve warm, or chill and pan-sear slices before serving.

name: Morcon
steps: Butterfly or pound the beef into a thin, even sheet. Marinate with the soy sauce, lemon juice and black pepper for at least 30 minutes.
Lay the beef flat and arrange strips of bacon, carrot, hotdog, cheese and hard-boiled egg down the center, with a smear of pickle relish.
Roll the beef tightly around the filling and tie with kitchen string or secure with toothpicks.
Dust the roll lightly with flour and sear it in cooking oil in a pot until browned on all sides. Set aside.
In the same pot, sauté the onion and garlic, add the tomato sauce, beef broth and bay leaf, then return the roll. Cover and simmer until tender, about 1.5 hours, turning occasionally.
Stir the liver spread into the sauce to thicken it. Rest the roll before slicing; beef should show no pink at the center.
Season the sauce with salt and pepper and spoon over the sliced roll.

name: Bopis
steps: Finely chop or mince the pork.
Heat cooking oil and sauté the onion and garlic until fragrant.
Add the pork and cook until browned, breaking it up as it cooks.
Stir in the vinegar and let it simmer uncovered a few minutes before stirring, then season with fish sauce and salt.
Add the finely chopped carrot, red and green bell pepper, and sliced bird's eye chili. Cook until the vegetables soften.
Simmer until the pork is fully cooked through, with no pink remaining, and the mixture is fairly dry. Serve hot.

name: Igado
steps: Cut the pork into strips.
Heat cooking oil, sauté the onion and garlic, then add the pork and cook until browned.
Add the soy sauce, vinegar and bay leaf. Bring to a boil, then simmer uncovered a few minutes before stirring.
Cover and simmer until the pork is tender, about 30 minutes, adding water as needed.
Add the beef liver, cut into strips, along with the red bell pepper and green peas. Liver cooks fast, so simmer just until it firms up, about 5 minutes, so it doesn't turn tough.
Season with black pepper and salt. Pork should show no pink; the liver should no longer look raw inside.

name: Asadong Baboy
steps: Slice the pork shoulder into strips. Marinate with the soy sauce, calamansi juice, crushed garlic and black pepper for at least 30 minutes.
Heat cooking oil, brown the pork, reserving the marinade, then set aside. Sauté the onion.
Return the pork, pour in the reserved marinade, the tomato sauce, bay leaf and enough water to cover. Bring to a boil, cover and simmer until tender, about 40 minutes.
Add the potato, cut into chunks, and simmer until it softens.
Stir in the liver spread until the sauce thickens.
Season with salt and pepper. Pork should be fully cooked with no pink remaining.

name: Bicol Express
steps: Cut the pork belly into small cubes.
In a pot, sauté the garlic, onion and ginger until fragrant, then add the pork and cook until browned.
Stir in the bagoong alamang and cook briefly to release its aroma.
Pour in the coconut milk, bring to a simmer, and cook uncovered until the pork is tender and the liquid reduces, about 30 minutes, stirring occasionally so it doesn't scorch.
Add the coconut cream and sliced bird's eye chili, to taste, and simmer until the sauce thickens and turns glossy.
Season with black pepper and all-in-one seasoning. Pork should be fully cooked through.

name: Binagoongang Baboy
steps: Cut the pork belly into cubes. Heat cooking oil and brown the pork, then set aside.
In the same pot, sauté the onion, garlic and chopped tomato until softened.
Return the pork, stir in the bagoong alamang, vinegar and brown sugar. Bring to a boil, then simmer uncovered a few minutes before stirring.
Cover and simmer until the pork is tender, about 40 minutes, adding water if needed.
Add the cubed eggplant and whole long green chilies, and simmer until the eggplant softens.
Stir in the coconut cream and season with all-in-one seasoning. Simmer briefly until the sauce thickens. Pork should be fully cooked through.

name: Lechon Belly
steps: Score the skin of the pork belly in a crosshatch, being careful not to cut into the meat.
Stuff the belly with the lemongrass, sliced onion, garlic and spring onion, then roll it up tightly, skin side out, and tie securely with kitchen string.
Rub the skin with a little soy sauce and let it air-dry, uncovered, in the refrigerator for several hours or overnight, so it roasts crisp.
Roast in a hot oven, turning occasionally, until the skin is deeply golden and crackling and the meat is cooked through, 1.5 to 2 hours depending on size.
While it roasts, mix a dipping sauce of the vinegar, soy sauce, chopped onion, garlic, sugar, black pepper and sliced bird's eye chili.
Let the roll rest for 10 minutes before slicing. Check that the center is no longer pink and reaches at least 63°C (145°F). Serve with the dipping sauce.

name: Chicken Inasal
steps: Marinate the chicken in pounded lemongrass, crushed garlic, ginger, vinegar, calamansi juice, brown sugar, salt and black pepper for at least 2 hours, or overnight for the best flavor.
Steep the annatto seeds in a few tablespoons of the marinade until the liquid turns deep orange, then strain out the seeds; this becomes the basting liquid.
Skewer the chicken and grill over medium-hot coals or a grill pan, turning regularly.
Baste with the annatto liquid every few minutes as it grills, tucking the bay leaf near the coals for aroma.
Grill until the skin is charred in spots and the chicken reaches 74°C (165°F) at the thickest part, with juices running clear.
Let rest a few minutes before serving.

name: Filipino Fried Chicken
steps: Marinate the chicken pieces in calamansi juice, soy sauce and black pepper for at least 30 minutes.
In a bowl, mix the flour, cornstarch, baking powder, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika and all-in-one seasoning.
Drain the chicken and dredge each piece in the flour mixture, pressing to coat well.
Heat plenty of cooking oil in a deep pot to about 175°C (350°F).
Fry the chicken in batches, without crowding, until golden and cooked through, about 10–12 minutes depending on piece size, turning halfway.
The chicken is done at 74°C (165°F) at the thickest part, with clear juices. Drain on a rack before serving.

name: Beef Salpicao
steps: Cut the beef into bite-sized cubes and season with salt and pepper.
Heat the olive oil in a hot pan and sear the beef cubes quickly on all sides, in batches so they brown rather than steam, then set aside.
Lower the heat, melt the butter in the same pan, and sauté the garlic until golden and fragrant, watching closely so it doesn't burn.
Return the beef to the pan with the worcestershire sauce, soy sauce and brown sugar, and toss to coat.
Cook briefly, just until the beef is heated through and glazed; searing hard and finishing fast keeps it tender.
Beef is safe at 63°C (145°F) with a brief rest, giving a pink, warmed-through center; cook longer if well-done is preferred. Sprinkle with chili flakes and serve.

name: Pata Tim
steps: Blanch the pork hock in boiling water for a few minutes to remove scum, then drain and rinse.
Heat cooking oil in a pot and brown the hock on all sides.
Add the soy sauce, chinese cooking wine, vinegar, sugar and star anise, along with enough water to cover.
Bring to a boil, then simmer uncovered a few minutes before stirring, so the vinegar mellows. Cover and simmer over low heat until the hock is very tender, 1.5 to 2 hours.
Add the mushroom and simmer another 10 minutes, then add the bok choy and cook just until wilted.
Uncover and reduce the sauce until it thickens and glazes the hock. The meat should be fully tender with no pink remaining near the bone.

name: Kare-Kare
steps: Place the oxtail in a pot with enough water to cover, bring to a boil, then skim off the scum. Simmer, covered, until very tender, 2 to 3 hours (a pressure cooker shortens this).
Toast the rice flour in a dry pan until lightly golden and fragrant, then set aside; this thickens the sauce.
In a separate pan, heat cooking oil and sauté the onion and garlic, then add the annatto seeds briefly to color the oil and strain them out.
Add the toasted rice flour and peanut butter to the annatto oil along with some of the oxtail's own cooking liquid, stirring until smooth and thick.
Pour this sauce into the pot with the oxtail. Add the banana heart, eggplant and string beans, and simmer until the vegetables are tender.
Add the bok choy last and cook just until wilted. Season with fish sauce and salt and pepper.
Serve with the bagoong alamang on the side for guests to add to taste. The oxtail should be fork-tender with no toughness left.

name: Callos
steps: Clean the tripe well and place it with the cow trotters in a pot of water with the vinegar, salt, bay leaf and black pepper. Boil until both are tender, 2 to 3 hours for the trotters (a pressure cooker speeds this up).
Drain and cut the tripe and trotter meat into bite-sized pieces.
In a separate pot, cook the bacon until it renders some fat, then add the onion, garlic and sliced bird's eye chili and sauté until fragrant.
Add the sliced chorizo and paprika, then stir in the tomato sauce and beef broth.
Add the cooked tripe and trotters along with the chickpeas, and simmer until the flavors meld, about 20 minutes.
Add the red and green bell pepper and green peas, and simmer until just tender.
Season with salt and pepper. The tripe and trotters should be thoroughly tender, not chewy.

name: Kalderetang Baboy
steps: Cut the pork shoulder into cubes and season with salt. Heat cooking oil and brown the pork, then set aside.
Sauté the onion and garlic. Return the pork, add the tomato sauce and a pork cube dissolved in water to cover. Bring to a boil, cover and simmer until nearly tender, about 45 minutes.
Add the potato and carrot, cut into chunks, and simmer until they soften.
Stir in the liver spread until the sauce thickens, then add the red and green bell pepper and green olives.
Simmer until the pork is tender with no pink remaining.
Stir in grated cheese until melted, adjust salt, and serve.

name: Adobong Pusit
steps: Clean the squid, separating the tubes and tentacles.
Heat cooking oil and sauté the garlic, onion and chopped tomato until softened.
Add the squid, vinegar, bay leaf, black pepper and whole long green chili. Bring to a boil, then simmer uncovered a few minutes before stirring.
Simmer gently. Squid turns rubbery if overcooked, so cook just until it's opaque throughout and tender, about 5 to 8 minutes for small pieces.
Season with all-in-one seasoning and reduce the sauce slightly if it looks thin.
Serve hot; the squid should be fully opaque with no translucent flesh remaining.

name: Filipino Chicken Curry
steps: Season the chicken with salt. Heat cooking oil in a pot and brown the chicken pieces, then set aside.
Sauté the onion, garlic and ginger until fragrant, then stir in the curry powder and turmeric and cook briefly until aromatic.
Return the chicken, add the ginataang gulay mix and enough water to loosen it into a sauce. Bring to a boil, cover and simmer until the chicken is nearly tender.
Add the potato, cut into chunks, and simmer until it softens.
Add the green peas and simmer a few more minutes.
The chicken is done at 74°C (165°F) at the thickest part. Adjust salt and serve.

name: Giniling na Baboy
steps: Heat cooking oil and sauté the onion and garlic until fragrant.
Add the pork, chopped or ground, and cook until browned, breaking it apart as it cooks.
Add the chopped tomato and cook until it softens, then season with fish sauce.
Add the diced potato and carrot with a little water, cover and simmer until they're tender.
Stir in the red and green bell pepper and raisins, and simmer a few more minutes.
Season with salt and pepper. Pork should be fully cooked through with no pink remaining.

name: Tortang Giniling
steps: Heat a little cooking oil and sauté the garlic, onion and chopped tomato until softened.
Add the ground pork and cook until browned, breaking it apart, until no pink remains.
Stir in the green peas and red and green bell pepper, and season with salt and black pepper. Let the filling cool slightly.
Beat the eggs in a bowl and mix in the cooked filling.
Heat a little more cooking oil in a pan and pour in portions of the egg mixture, spreading into rounds.
Cook until the bottom sets and turns golden, then flip carefully and cook the other side until the egg is fully set and the filling reaches 71°C (160°F).

name: Adobo Flakes
steps: Cut the pork shoulder into chunks and place in a pot with the soy sauce, vinegar, bay leaf, black pepper and enough water to cover.
Bring to a boil, then simmer uncovered a few minutes before stirring, so the vinegar mellows. Cover and simmer until the pork is very tender, about 45 minutes.
Remove the pork, let it cool slightly, then shred it into small pieces with two forks. Reserve the braising liquid.
Heat cooking oil in a pan and fry the shredded pork with minced garlic until the edges turn crisp and golden.
Splash in a little of the reserved braising liquid and let it reduce, coating the flakes. Season with all-in-one seasoning.
Cook until crisp and heated through, with no pink remaining. Serve hot.

name: Adobong Baka
steps: Cut the beef into cubes and season with all-in-one seasoning.
Heat cooking oil in a pot and brown the beef, then set aside.
Sauté the garlic, then return the beef along with the bay leaf, black pepper, vinegar and sliced bird's eye chili. Bring to a boil, then simmer uncovered a few minutes before stirring.
Add enough water to cover, cover the pot, and simmer until the beef is tender, about 1 hour.
Stir in the all purpose cream and simmer uncovered until the sauce thickens slightly.
Beef should show no pink at the center. Adjust seasoning and serve.

name: Lengua Estofado
steps: Boil the ox tongue with a beef cube in a pot, using just enough water to submerge it, until a knife slides in with no resistance, roughly 1.5 to 2 hours.
While it's still hot, scrape off the coarse outer skin with a paring knife. It comes away easily now but grips hard once cool. Slice the peeled tongue into rounds.
Coat the rounds lightly in flour and brown them in hot cooking oil on both sides, then lift them out.
Using that same oil, soften the onion and garlic, then stir in the chopped tomato and cook it down.
Pour in the white wine, soy sauce, vinegar and brown sugar, tuck in the bay leaf, and bring back the tongue rounds along with the liquid they were braised in.
Toss in the mushroom and green olives, and let everything simmer together until the sauce reduces to a glossy coating and the tongue turns fork-tender.
Finish with salt to taste; the meat should give easily under a fork, with no chew left in it.

name: Chicken Pastel
steps: Marinate the chicken breast in the soy sauce and lemon juice for at least 15 minutes, then cut into bite-sized pieces.
Heat cooking oil in a pot and cook the chicken until lightly browned, then set aside.
In the same pot, melt the butter and sauté the onion, garlic and sliced chorizo. Stir in some of the flour to form a light roux, then gradually whisk in the evaporated milk to make a creamy sauce.
Return the chicken and add the carrot, green peas, mushroom and sliced vienna sausage. Simmer until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce thickens. Season with salt and pepper.
For the crust, cut cold butter into the remaining flour, sugar and salt until crumbly, then bind with the vinegar and a beaten egg into a dough, and roll it out.
Spoon the filling into a baking dish, top with the rolled dough, brush with beaten egg, and bake until the crust is golden.
Chicken should reach 74°C (165°F); check the filling before baking, since baking mainly browns the already-cooked filling.

name: Beef Pares
steps: Place the beef in a pot with the onion, bay leaf, black pepper and salt, and enough water to cover. Boil, skimming off scum, until the beef is tender, about 1.5 hours.
In a separate pot, heat cooking oil and sauté more onion, garlic and ginger. Add the soy sauce, brown sugar and star anise, along with some of the beef's own cooking liquid.
Add the cooked beef, cut into bite-sized pieces, and simmer in this sauce until it thickens slightly and coats the beef. Season with salt and pepper.
For the garlic rice, heat cooking oil in a pan and fry minced garlic until golden. Add the cooked rice and toss until evenly coated and heated through, seasoning with salt and pepper.
The beef should be tender with no toughness and fully cooked through.
Serve the beef and sauce over or alongside the garlic rice, topped with sliced spring onion.

name: Chicken Tapa
steps: Marinate the chicken thighs in the soy sauce, lemon juice, crushed garlic, brown sugar, salt and black pepper for at least 30 minutes, or overnight for deeper flavor.
Heat cooking oil in a pan over medium heat.
Cook the marinated chicken, skin side down first, until browned, then flip and continue cooking.
Lower the heat if the marinade starts to darken too fast, and cook through, basting occasionally with the pan juices.
Chicken is done at 74°C (165°F) with clear juices and no pink near the bone.
Rest briefly before serving.

name: Pininyahang Manok
steps: Season the chicken with salt and pepper. Heat cooking oil in a pot and brown the chicken pieces, then set aside.
Sauté the onion and garlic until fragrant. Return the chicken, pour in the pineapple juice and enough water to half-cover, and bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer until the chicken is nearly tender, about 20 minutes.
Add the canned pineapple chunks and sliced red bell pepper, and simmer a few more minutes until the pepper softens.
Stir in the all purpose cream and simmer uncovered until the sauce thickens slightly.
The chicken should reach 74°C (165°F) at the thickest part. Season with salt and pepper and serve.

name: Rellenong Manok
steps: Debone the chicken, keeping the skin intact, and marinate it inside and out with the calamansi juice, soy sauce and black pepper for at least 30 minutes.
For the stuffing, mix the pork with the chopped pineapple, onion, carrot, breadcrumbs, grated cheese, raisins, a beaten egg, mayonnaise and banana ketchup. Season with salt and black pepper.
Lay the deboned chicken skin-side down, spoon the stuffing down the center along with the hard-boiled eggs, then fold the chicken back around the filling and tie it closed into a roll.
Rub the outside with softened butter and place in a roasting pan.
Roast in a moderate oven, basting occasionally with the pan juices, until the skin is golden and both the chicken and the pork stuffing are cooked through, about 1.5 hours depending on size.
The stuffing contains raw pork and egg, so check the center reaches at least 74°C (165°F), same as the chicken, with no pink remaining.
Rest for 10 minutes before slicing into rounds.

name: Sinuglaw
steps: Grill the pork belly over hot coals or a grill pan until charred and cooked through, then let it cool and chop into small cubes. It should show no pink and reach at least 63°C (145°F).
Cut the tuna into small cubes; use tuna that was previously frozen for raw service, since vinegar and lemon juice do not kill parasites. Keep it cold while you work.

Toss the tuna cubes with the vinegar, lemon juice and salt, and let sit until the flesh turns opaque at the edges. This dish cures it briefly rather than cooking it through, so use only fish you'd eat raw.
Combine the chopped grilled pork with the cured tuna in a bowl.
Add the chopped onion, ginger, sliced cucumber, and sliced long green chili and bird's eye chili. Toss to combine.
Adjust salt and vinegar to taste and serve immediately, chilled.

name: Sinigang na Hipon
steps: In a pot, combine the tomato, onion and radish with enough water to cover, and bring to a boil.
Add the tamarind and simmer until it softens, then mash it against the side of the pot to release its sour flavor into the liquid.
Add the eggplant and string beans and simmer until they begin to soften.
Add the shrimp, okra and long green chili, and simmer just until the shrimp turn pink and opaque, a few minutes.
Add the kangkong last and cook just until wilted.
Season with fish sauce to taste. Shrimp are done when they curl and turn fully pink, with no gray, translucent flesh left.

name: Sinigang na Bangus
steps: Combine the tomato and onion in a pot with enough water to cover, and bring to a boil.
Add the tamarind and simmer until soft, then mash it to release the sour flavor into the liquid.
Add the string beans and okra and simmer until they begin to soften.
Slide in the milkfish pieces and long green chili, and simmer gently until the fish is opaque and flakes easily, a few minutes.
Add the kangkong last and cook just until wilted.
Season with fish sauce and black pepper. The fish should be opaque all the way through, with no translucent center.

name: Sinigang na Sugpo
steps: Combine the onion, tomato and lemongrass with enough water to cover in a pot, and bring to a boil.
Add the taro, cut into chunks, and simmer until it starts to soften.
Add the tamarind and simmer until soft, then mash it into the liquid for its sour flavor.
Stir in the coconut cream and long green chili, and simmer a few minutes.
Add the shrimp and simmer just until they turn pink and opaque.
Add the kangkong last and cook just until wilted. Shrimp should show no gray, translucent flesh before serving.

name: Rellenong Alimasag
steps: Steam or boil the crab until fully cooked, the shell turning bright orange-red, then let it cool and pick out the meat, reserving the shells.
In a pan, heat cooking oil and sauté the onion, tomato and long green chili until softened.
Add the crab meat, breadcrumbs, chopped parsley, garlic powder, salt and black pepper, and mix well, binding it with a beaten egg.
Separately, boil the potato and carrot, cut into small dice, until tender, then fold them into the crab mixture.
Spoon the mixture back into the reserved crab shells, packing it in.
Heat more cooking oil in a pan and pan-fry the stuffed shells, filling side down, until golden and heated through.
The filling was mixed with raw egg, so fry until it is firm throughout and reaches 74°C (165°F) before serving.

name: Daing na Bangus
steps: Butterfly the milkfish, removing the backbone so it lies flat.
Marinate it in a mixture of vinegar, crushed garlic, black pepper and salt for at least 30 minutes, or overnight in the refrigerator.
Heat cooking oil in a pan over medium heat.
Fry the milkfish, skin side down first, until golden and crisp, then flip and cook the other side.
Cook until the flesh is opaque and flakes easily with a fork, with no translucent center.
Drain briefly and serve hot.

name: Paksiw na Isda
steps: In a pot, combine the vinegar with an equal amount of water, the sliced ginger, garlic and onion. Bring to a boil.
Add the fish in a single layer, along with the bitter gourd and long green chili.
Season with salt and black pepper. Cover and simmer gently, without stirring too much since fish breaks apart easily, until cooked through, 10–15 minutes depending on thickness.
The fish is done when the flesh is opaque and flakes easily, with no translucent center.
Simmer a little longer, uncovered, to reduce the sauce.
Serve hot, straight from the pot.

name: Paksiw na Bangus
steps: In a pot, combine the vinegar with a little water, the sliced ginger, garlic and onion, and bring to a boil.
Add the milkfish and eggplant, cut into chunks, along with the whole bird's eye chilies.
Season with salt and black pepper. Cover and simmer gently, without stirring too much, until the fish is cooked through, about 10–15 minutes.
The fish is done when the flesh is opaque and flakes easily, with no translucent center, and the eggplant is tender.
If you'd like the sauce to reduce further, simmer uncovered a few more minutes, then finish with a drizzle of cooking oil.
Serve hot.

name: Escabecheng Isda
steps: Season the fish with salt and black pepper.
Heat cooking oil in a pan and fry the fish until golden and cooked through, the flesh opaque and flaking easily. Set aside.
In the same pan, sauté the garlic and onion until fragrant, then add the red bell pepper and cook briefly until just tender.
Add the vinegar, sugar and a little water, and bring to a boil, then simmer a couple of minutes until slightly syrupy.
Season the sauce with salt to taste.
Pour the sweet-and-sour sauce over the fried fish and serve immediately.

name: Kinilaw na Tanigue
steps: Use tuna that was previously frozen for raw service; vinegar and calamansi do not kill parasites. Keep it cold while you work.
Cut the tuna into small, even cubes.
Toss the tuna with the vinegar and calamansi juice, and let it sit for several minutes until the flesh turns opaque at the edges; this cures rather than fully cooks it.
Add the chopped ginger, onion and sliced bird's eye chili, and season with salt and black pepper.
Toss well and adjust the vinegar, calamansi and salt to taste.
Serve immediately, chilled. Since the center stays raw, use only fish you'd eat raw, and keep it cold until served.

name: Ginataang Tilapia
steps: Heat cooking oil in a pan and sauté the garlic, onion and ginger until fragrant.
Pour in the coconut milk and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the tilapia, long green chili and bird's eye chili, and season with fish sauce and black pepper.
Simmer gently, without boiling hard, until the fish is cooked through and the sauce reduces slightly, about 10 minutes.
Add the spinach and cook just until wilted.
The fish should be opaque throughout, with no translucent center, before serving.

name: Inihaw na Bangus
steps: Butterfly the milkfish and season it with salt, black pepper and calamansi juice, rubbing the marinade inside and out.
Stuff the cavity with chopped tomato, onion and ginger.
Let it marinate about 15 minutes while you heat a grill or grill pan.
Grill the fish over medium heat, turning once, until the skin chars slightly and the flesh is opaque and flakes easily.
Watch it closely. Milkfish dries out fast once it passes opaque.
Serve hot with extra calamansi on the side.

name: Pritong Tilapia
steps: Clean the tilapia and pat it dry.
Season it inside and out with the all-in-one seasoning, and let it sit for a few minutes.
Heat plenty of cooking oil in a pan over medium-high heat.
Fry the tilapia until golden and crisp on one side, then carefully flip and fry the other side.
Cook until the flesh is opaque and flakes easily with a fork, with no translucent center near the bone.
Drain briefly on a rack before serving.

name: Sweet and Sour Fish
steps: Cut the tilapia into pieces and season with soy sauce and salt and pepper.
Beat the egg, and mix the flour with the cornstarch. Dip the fish in the egg, then coat in the flour mixture.
Heat cooking oil and fry the fish until golden and cooked through, with opaque flesh; drain and set aside.
In a separate pan, sauté the onion and red bell pepper briefly, then add the pineapple juice, vinegar, banana ketchup and brown sugar, and bring to a simmer.
Mix a little more cornstarch with water and stir it in to thicken the sauce, seasoning with salt.
Pour the sauce over the fried fish just before serving, so it stays crisp.

name: Ginataang Hipon
steps: Heat cooking oil in a pan and sauté the onion, ginger and garlic until fragrant.
Pour in the coconut milk and bring to a gentle simmer.
Season with fish sauce and add the whole bird's eye chilies.
Add the shrimp and simmer just until they turn pink and opaque, a few minutes; overcooking makes them tough.
Season with salt and pepper.
Shrimp should show no gray or translucent flesh before serving.

name: Halabos na Hipon
steps: Heat the butter and olive oil in a wide pan over medium heat, and sauté the garlic until fragrant.
Add the shrimp, still in their shells, and toss to coat.
Pour in the lemon-lime soda and let it come to a simmer.
Cover and steam-cook the shrimp until they turn pink and opaque, a few minutes, tossing once or twice.
Uncover and let the liquid reduce slightly, coating the shrimp.
Season with chili flakes and salt and pepper. Shrimp should show no gray, translucent flesh before serving.

name: Sinigang na Salmon
steps: Heat cooking oil in a pot and sauté the garlic, ginger, onion and tomato until softened.
Add enough water to cover, then add the radish and string beans and simmer until they start to soften.
Add the tamarind and simmer until soft, then mash it into the liquid for its sour flavor.
Add the okra and long green chili, and season with fish sauce and brown sugar.
Slide in the salmon and simmer gently until it's just cooked through and flakes easily, a few minutes; salmon overcooks quickly.
Add the kangkong last and cook just until wilted. The salmon should be opaque throughout before serving.

name: Pesang Isda
steps: Heat cooking oil in a pot and sauté the onion, ginger and garlic until fragrant.
Add the rice and enough water to make a light gruel, and bring to a boil; simmer until the rice is soft and the liquid turns slightly milky.
Season with fish sauce, salt and black pepper.
Slide in the fish and simmer gently until it's cooked through and flakes easily, a few minutes.
Add the bok choy and cook just until wilted.
Top with sliced spring onion. The fish should be opaque all the way through before serving.

name: Tinolang Isda
steps: In a pot, combine the onion, ginger and lemongrass with enough water to cover, and bring to a boil.
Add the tomato and simmer a few minutes until it softens.
Season with fish sauce, then add the tuna and fish along with the long green chili.
Simmer gently until the fish is cooked through and flakes easily, a few minutes.
Add the chili leaves and spring onion and cook just until wilted.
The fish should be opaque throughout, with no translucent center, before serving.

name: Adobong Hipon
steps: Heat cooking oil in a pan and sauté the garlic until fragrant.
Add the soy sauce, vinegar, bay leaf and black pepper, and bring to a boil, then simmer uncovered a few minutes before stirring, so the vinegar mellows.
Pour in the coconut milk and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the shrimp and simmer just until they turn pink and opaque, a few minutes.
Season with salt to taste.
Shrimp should show no gray, translucent flesh before serving.

name: Bangus Belly
steps: In a pot, combine the tomato, onion and radish with enough water to cover, and bring to a boil.
Add the tamarind and simmer until soft, then mash it into the liquid for its sour flavor.
Stir in the miso until dissolved, then add the okra and long green chili.
Slide in the milkfish belly pieces and simmer gently until they're cooked through and opaque, a few minutes; belly cuts are fatty and cook quickly.
Add the mustard greens last and cook just until wilted.
Season with fish sauce. The fish should be opaque throughout before serving.

name: Pinangat na Isda
steps: In a pot, combine the tomato and sliced kamias with a little water, and bring to a simmer; the kamias adds a sour edge.
Season with salt and black pepper.
Lay the fish in the pot in a single layer.
Cover and simmer gently, without stirring too much, until the fish is cooked through, about 10–15 minutes.
The fish should be opaque throughout and flake easily, with no translucent center.
Serve hot, straight from the pot, with the sauce spooned over.

name: Sarciadong Isda
steps: Season the fish with the all-in-one seasoning.
Heat cooking oil in a pan and fry the fish until golden and cooked through, with opaque flesh. Set aside.
In the same pan, sauté the garlic, onion and tomato until the tomato breaks down into a light sauce.
Add a little water and season with black pepper, then bring to a simmer.
Return the fried fish to the pan, then drizzle in the beaten egg and let it set into ribbons without stirring too much.
Cook until the egg is fully set with no runny parts, then top with spring onion and serve.

name: Ginataang Alimasag
steps: Clean the crab and cut it into halves or quarters.
Heat cooking oil in a pot and sauté the garlic, onion and ginger until fragrant.
Stir in the bagoong alamang and cook briefly to release its aroma.
Pour in the coconut milk and add the crab and whole bird's eye chilies. Simmer until the shell turns bright orange-red and the meat is opaque throughout.
Season with fish sauce and black pepper.
Add the spinach and cook just until wilted before serving.

name: Chili Crab
steps: Clean the crab and cut it into halves or quarters.
Melt the butter in a wok or pan and sauté the garlic and ginger until fragrant.
Add the chili paste and chopped tomato, and cook until the tomato breaks down.
Add the crab, season with brown sugar and all-in-one seasoning, and add a little water. Cover and simmer until the shell turns bright orange-red and the meat is opaque throughout, about 10 minutes.
Drizzle in the beaten egg and let it set into ribbons through the sauce without over-stirring.
Season with black pepper, top with spring onion, and serve once the egg is fully set.

name: Calamares
steps: Clean the squid and slice it into rings.
Season the rings with salt and black pepper.
Set up a dredge of flour, then beaten egg, then breadcrumbs, coating each ring in that order.
Heat plenty of cooking oil in a pot until hot.
Fry the squid rings in batches, briefly, until golden; a minute or two is usually enough. Overcooking turns squid rubbery.
Drain on a rack. The squid should be fully opaque, with no translucent flesh, before serving.

name: Inihaw na Panga ng Tuna
steps: In a pot, combine the tomato and onion with enough water to cover, and bring to a boil.
Add the tamarind and simmer until soft, then mash it into the liquid for its sour flavor.
Add the eggplant and string beans and simmer until they begin to soften.
Slide in the tuna jaw, along with the okra and long green chili, and simmer gently until the fish is cooked through, opaque near the bone.
Add the kangkong last and cook just until wilted.
Season with fish sauce. Check that the thickest part of the jaw is opaque, with no translucent flesh, before serving.

name: Ginataang Tinapa
steps: Heat cooking oil in a pot and sauté the garlic and onion until fragrant.
Stir in the bagoong alamang and cook briefly, then add the coconut milk and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the jackfruit and smoked fish, flaked into pieces, and simmer, stirring occasionally, until the jackfruit softens and the sauce reduces, about 20 minutes.
Season with black pepper, salt and a splash of vinegar.
Add the moringa leaves and simmer just until wilted.
Simmer until the sauce thickens and turns glossy and the smoked fish is fully warmed through, then serve.

name: Sinigang na Baboy
steps: In a pot, place the pork belly with the onion, tomato and enough water to cover. Bring to a boil, skimming off scum, then simmer until the pork is nearly tender, 30–40 minutes.
Add the tamarind and simmer until soft, then mash it into the liquid for its sour flavor.
Add the radish and eggplant, and simmer until they begin to soften.
Add the string beans, okra and long green chili, and simmer a few more minutes.
Add the kangkong last and cook just until wilted.
Season with fish sauce. Pork should be fully cooked through, with no pink remaining.

name: Sinigang na Baka
steps: Place the beef in a pot with the onion and tomato, and enough water to cover. Bring to a boil, skimming off scum, then simmer until the beef is nearly tender, about 1 hour.
Add the taro, cut into chunks, and simmer until it starts to soften.
Add the tamarind and simmer until soft, then mash it into the liquid for its sour flavor.
Add the eggplant, string beans and long green chili, and simmer until tender.
Add the kangkong last and cook just until wilted.
Season with fish sauce. The beef should be tender with no toughness left.

name: Bulalo
steps: Place the beef shank in a large pot with the onion, a beef cube and enough water to cover generously. Bring to a boil, skimming off scum.
Lower the heat and simmer, covered, until the beef and marrow are very tender, 2 to 3 hours (a pressure cooker shortens this).
Add the corn, cut into rounds, and simmer until tender.
Add the green beans and simmer a few minutes.
Add the napa cabbage last and cook just until wilted.
Season with fish sauce and black pepper. The beef should pull apart easily, with the marrow soft enough to scoop.

name: Nilagang Baka
steps: Place the beef shank and beef in a large pot with the onion and enough water to cover. Bring to a boil, skimming off scum.
Lower the heat and simmer, covered, until the beef is tender, about 1.5 to 2 hours.
Add the potato and corn, cut into chunks and rounds, and simmer until tender.
Add the green beans and simmer a few minutes.
Add the cabbage last and cook just until wilted.
Season with fish sauce, salt and black pepper, and top with spring onion. The beef should be fully tender.

name: Nilagang Baboy
steps: Submerge the pork belly and pork in a pot along with the onion, using just enough water to cover everything, and set it over high heat, skimming off any scum as it rises.
Once it's boiling, turn the heat down low, cover the pot, and let it simmer until the pork is nearly done, roughly 40 minutes.
Cut the potato and banana into chunks, drop them in, and cook until they turn soft.
Stir in the cabbage right at the end, just long enough for it to wilt.
Finish with salt, black pepper and a drizzle of cooking oil stirred through.
The pork should be cooked all the way through, with no pink left inside.

name: Tinolang Manok
steps: Heat cooking oil in a pot and sauté the garlic, onion and ginger until fragrant.
Add the chicken and cook until it changes color on the outside, then continue until it reaches 74°C (165°F) at the thickest piece.
Add a chicken cube dissolved in enough water to cover, and bring to a boil. Simmer until the chicken is nearly cooked through.
Add the green papaya, cut into wedges, and simmer until it softens.
Add the moringa and chili leaves and cook just until wilted.
Season with fish sauce and black pepper. Chicken should reach 74°C (165°F), with no pink at the bone.

name: Sopas
steps: Heat cooking oil in a pot and sauté the garlic and onion until fragrant.
Stir in the saute seasoning and enough water to make a light stock, and bring to a boil.
Add the macaroni and carrot, and simmer until the macaroni is tender.
Season with the all-in-one seasoning.
Add the cabbage and cook just until wilted.
Stir in the evaporated milk and simmer briefly until heated through and creamy; don't let it boil hard once it's added, or it can curdle.

name: La Paz Batchoy
steps: Place the pork and small intestine in a pot with enough water to cover. Boil, skimming off scum, until tender, about 45 minutes.
Remove the meats, let cool slightly, then slice thinly. Keep the cooking liquid as your soup base.
Return the sliced pork and intestine to the pot, and add the pork liver, sliced thinly; liver cooks quickly, so add it near the end.
Season with the bagoong alamang, onion powder, sugar, salt and black pepper. Simmer just until the liver is firm and no longer pink inside, a few minutes.
Cook the fresh egg noodles separately in boiling water until tender, then divide into bowls.
Ladle the hot liquid and meats over the noodles, and top with pork cracklings, sliced garlic and spring onion.

name: Pancit Molo
steps: In a bowl, mix the finely chopped pork and chicken with the finely chopped water chestnut and carrot, plus a little garlic, soy sauce, salt and black pepper.
Wrap small portions of the filling in the wonton wrapper, sealing the edges with a dab of water.
Heat cooking oil in a pot and sauté the onion, garlic and bay leaf until fragrant.
Pour in the homemade broth and bring to a boil, then season with fish sauce and salt and pepper.
Drop the wrapped dumplings into the simmering liquid and cook until they float, the chicken reaches 74°C (165°F), and the filling has no pink remaining, about 8–10 minutes.
Top with sliced spring onion and serve hot.

name: Goto
steps: Clean the tripe well and place it in a pot with the beef, salt and enough water to cover. Boil, skimming off scum, until both are tender, 1.5 to 2 hours (a pressure cooker speeds this up).
Drain, reserving the cooking liquid, and cut the tripe and beef into small pieces.
Heat cooking oil in a pot and sauté the onion, garlic and ginger until fragrant.
Add the glutinous rice and toast briefly, then pour in the broth and the reserved cooking liquid, and bring to a boil.
Add the tripe and beef, and simmer, stirring occasionally so the rice doesn't stick, until the rice breaks down and the soup thickens, 20–30 minutes.
Season with fish sauce and salt and pepper. Top with garlic, spring onion and a squeeze of calamansi. The tripe should be tender, not chewy.

name: Arroz Caldo
steps: Heat cooking oil in a pot and sauté the onion, garlic and ginger until fragrant.
Add the chicken and cook until it changes color on the outside, then continue until it reaches 74°C (165°F) at the thickest piece.
Add the rice and toast briefly, then add a bouillon cube dissolved in enough water to cover generously.
Bring to a boil, then simmer, stirring occasionally so the rice doesn't stick, until it breaks down and the soup thickens and the chicken is cooked through, 25–30 minutes.
Season with fish sauce and salt and pepper.
Fry extra garlic in cooking oil until golden and crisp for topping. Ladle into bowls, top with sliced hard-boiled egg, fried garlic, spring onion and a squeeze of calamansi.

name: Papaitan
steps: Cut the beef into bite-sized pieces. Heat cooking oil in a pot and sauté the garlic, onion and ginger until fragrant.
Add the beef and cook until it changes color on the outside.
Add enough water to cover, bring to a boil, skim off scum, then simmer, covered, until the beef is tender, 1 to 1.5 hours.
Add the tamarind and simmer until soft, then mash it into the liquid for its sour flavor. Add the long green chili.
Season with fish sauce, brown sugar and black pepper.
Finish with a squeeze of calamansi. The beef should be tender, with no toughness left.

name: Ginataang Munggo
steps: Rinse the mung beans and place them in a pot with enough water to cover generously. Boil until they soften and start to split, 30–40 minutes.
Add the glutinous rice and enough water to keep everything loose, and simmer until the rice is tender and the mixture thickens, stirring occasionally so it doesn't stick.
Stir in the coconut milk and sugar, and simmer a few more minutes.
Stir in the coconut cream last, off the heat, so it doesn't separate.
The mung beans and rice should be fully soft, with no hard bite left.
Serve warm.

name: Lugaw
steps: Heat cooking oil in a pot and sauté the garlic, ginger and onion until fragrant.
Add the glutinous rice and toast briefly, then add enough water to cover generously and bring to a boil.
Add a pinch of safflower for color, then simmer, stirring occasionally so the rice doesn't stick, until it breaks down into a thick porridge, 25–30 minutes.
Season with the all-in-one seasoning and black pepper.
Crack the egg into the simmering porridge and stir it through until fully set, with no runny egg remaining.
Fry extra garlic until golden for topping. Ladle into bowls and top with pork cracklings, fried garlic, spring onion and a squeeze of calamansi.

name: Tinolang Tahong
steps: Scrub the mussels well and discard any that are open and don't close when tapped.
Heat cooking oil in a pot and sauté the garlic, onion and ginger until fragrant.
Add enough water to cover generously and bring to a boil. Season with fish sauce and black pepper.
Add the mussels and long green chili, cover, and simmer just until the shells open, a few minutes.
Discard any mussels that stay closed after cooking. They were not safe to eat.
Add the chili leaves and cook just until wilted, then serve hot.

name: Sinabawang Gulay
steps: In a pot, combine the ginger, lemongrass and onion with enough water to cover, and bring to a boil.
Add the round scad and simmer until it's cooked through and flakes easily.
Add the squash and eggplant, cut into chunks, and simmer until they begin to soften.
Add the sponge gourd and okra, and season with the all-in-one seasoning.
Add the moringa and jute leaves last and cook just until wilted.
Top with spring onion. The fish should be opaque throughout, with no translucent center, before serving.

name: Misua with Patola
steps: Heat cooking oil in a pot and sauté the garlic and onion until fragrant.
Stir in the saute seasoning and add enough water to make a light soup base. Bring to a boil.
Add the sponge gourd, cut into chunks, and simmer until it softens.
Season with the all-in-one seasoning.
Add the wheat vermicelli and simmer just until tender, a couple of minutes. It cooks fast and turns mushy if left too long.
Serve hot immediately.

name: Chicken Sotanghon Soup
steps: Heat cooking oil in a pot and sauté the onion, garlic and ginger until fragrant.
Add the chicken wings and cook until they change color on the outside.
Add the annatto seeds briefly to color the oil, then pour in the chicken broth and bring to a boil. Simmer until the chicken is cooked through.
Add the carrot and celery, and simmer until they soften.
Add the glass noodles and napa cabbage, and simmer just until the noodles are tender.

Season with fish sauce and salt and pepper. Fry extra garlic until golden for topping. Ladle into bowls, top with sliced hard-boiled egg, fried garlic and spring onion. Chicken should reach 74°C (165°F).

name: Pocherong Baka
steps: Cut the beef into serving pieces. Heat cooking oil in a pot and brown the beef and sliced chorizo, then set aside.
In the same pot, sauté the onion, garlic and chopped tomato until softened.
Return the beef and chorizo, add the tomato sauce and enough water to cover. Bring to a boil, skim off scum, cover and simmer until the beef is nearly tender, about 1 hour.
Add the potato and banana, cut into chunks, along with the chickpeas, and simmer until they soften.
Add the string beans and simmer a few minutes, then add the cabbage and bok choy last and cook just until wilted.
Season with fish sauce and black pepper. The beef should be tender, with no toughness left.

name: Balbacua
steps: Clean the cow trotters well. Heat cooking oil in a pot and sauté the garlic, onion and ginger until fragrant.
Add the trotters and cook until they change color on the outside, then add the lemongrass and a beef cube dissolved in enough water to cover generously.

Add the annatto seeds for color, bring to a boil, skim off scum, then cover and simmer over low heat until the trotters are very tender and gelatinous, 3 to 4 hours (a pressure cooker shortens this considerably).
Stir in the tomato sauce and salted black beans, and simmer another 15 minutes.
Add the green bell pepper and simmer until tender.
Season with fish sauce and black pepper, and top with spring onion. The trotters should be soft enough to pull apart easily.

name: Cansi
steps: Place the beef shank in a pot with the onion, garlic, lemongrass and a beef cube dissolved in enough water to cover generously.
Bring to a boil, skim off scum, then add the annatto seeds for color. Cover and simmer until the beef is nearly tender, about 1.5 hours.
Add the tamarind and simmer until soft, then mash it into the liquid for its sour flavor.
Add the jackfruit and tomato, and simmer until the jackfruit softens.
Add the long green chili and bird's eye chili, to taste.
Season with fish sauce. The beef should be tender, with no toughness left.

name: Sinampalukang Manok
steps: Heat cooking oil in a pot and sauté the onion, tomato and ginger until softened.
Add the chicken and cook until it changes color on the outside.
Add enough water to cover, bring to a boil, then simmer until the chicken is nearly cooked through.
Add the tamarind and simmer until soft, then mash it into the liquid for its sour flavor.
Add the eggplant and string beans, and simmer until tender.
Add the spinach last and cook just until wilted. Season with fish sauce. Chicken should reach 74°C (165°F), with no pink at the bone.

name: Pesang Baboy at Manok
steps: Place the pork belly and chicken in a pot with the ginger and enough water to cover. Bring to a boil, skim off scum.
Lower the heat and simmer, covered, until the pork and chicken are nearly tender, about 30–40 minutes.
Add the potato, cut into chunks, and simmer until it softens.
Add the long green chili and season with fish sauce and black pepper.
Add the napa cabbage last and cook just until wilted.
The pork and chicken should be fully cooked through, the chicken reaching 74°C (165°F), with no pink remaining in either.

name: Pinakbet
steps: Heat cooking oil in a pot and sauté the garlic, onion, ginger and tomato until softened.
Stir in the bagoong alamang and a shrimp cube dissolved in a little water, and cook briefly until fragrant.
Add the sweet potato and squash first, since they take longest, and cook a few minutes.
Add the eggplant, bitter gourd, string beans and okra, and cook until just tender. Do not overcook them, or they turn mushy and lose their color.
Add the lechon kawali and toss to combine, warming it through.
Season with black pepper and serve.

name: Ginataang Langka
steps: Heat cooking oil in a pot and sauté the garlic, onion and ginger until fragrant.
Add the pork belly and cook until it changes color on the outside and renders some fat.
Stir in the bagoong alamang and season with the all-in-one seasoning.
Add the jackfruit and enough water to keep things from sticking, and simmer until the pork and jackfruit are tender, 25–30 minutes.
Stir in the coconut milk and simmer until the sauce thickens slightly.
The pork should be fully cooked through, with no pink remaining.

name: Laing
steps: In a pot, layer the dried taro leaves without stirring them in yet. Stirring too early tears the leaves and can leave the dish scratchy on the tongue.
Add the pork, garlic, ginger, onion and bird's eye chili on top.
Pour the ginataang gulay mix over everything, and bring to a gentle simmer.
Simmer, uncovered at first and without stirring, until the liquid reduces and the leaves soften, 30–40 minutes.
Once the leaves have softened, stir gently to combine and continue simmering until the sauce thickens and turns richly oily on top, and the pork is fully cooked through.
Serve hot; the dish should look thick and dry, not soupy.

name: Chopsuey
steps: Heat cooking oil in a wok and sauté the garlic and onion until fragrant.
Stir in the saute seasoning and add a splash of water to build a light sauce.
Add the carrot and cauliflower first, since they take longest, and stir-fry a few minutes.
Add the chayote and string beans, and stir-fry until they begin to soften.
Add the red bell pepper, snow peas and cabbage last, and stir-fry just until bright and still crisp.
Serve immediately while the vegetables are still crisp-tender.

name: Ginataang Gulay
steps: Heat cooking oil in a pot and sauté the onion and garlic until fragrant.
Add the pork belly and cook until it changes color on the outside.
Stir in the bagoong alamang, then add the coconut milk and squash, cut into chunks. Simmer until the squash starts to soften and the pork is nearly tender.
Add the jackfruit and eggplant, and simmer until tender.
Add the green beans and shrimp, and simmer just until the shrimp turn pink and opaque and the pork is fully cooked through.
Season with salt and pepper.

name: Ginisang Monggo
steps: Rinse the mung beans and place them in a pot with enough water to cover generously. Boil until soft and starting to split, 30–40 minutes.
Meanwhile, in a pan, sauté the garlic, onion and tomato until softened.
Add the anchovies and cook briefly until they break down into the aromatics.
Stir the sautéed mixture into the cooked mung beans, and simmer a few more minutes.
Season with fish sauce and black pepper.
Add the spinach last and cook just until wilted.

name: Adobong Kangkong
steps: Heat cooking oil in a pan and sauté the garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the soy sauce and vinegar, and simmer without stirring for a minute, to cook off the vinegar's raw sharpness.
Stir in the kangkong and toss to coat in the sauce.
Cook just until the kangkong wilts. It cooks fast, so do not leave it on the heat too long or it turns mushy.
Season with black pepper.
Serve immediately.

name: Ampalaya con Carne
steps: Slice the beef thinly and marinate briefly in soy sauce, a little of the cornstarch and a pinch of salt and pepper.
Heat cooking oil in a wok and sear the beef over high heat until just cooked through, then set aside.
In the same wok, sauté the garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the bitter gourd and stir-fry until just tender but still bright green.
Return the beef to the wok, add the oyster sauce, sugar and a splash of water, and toss to combine.
Finish with a drizzle of sesame oil and season with salt and pepper.

name: Ginisang Ampalaya
steps: Heat cooking oil in a pan and sauté the garlic, onion and tomato until softened.
Stir in the tomato sauce and a splash of water, and simmer briefly.
Add the bitter gourd and cook until just tender but still bright green.
Season with fish sauce, sugar and salt and pepper. The sugar balances the bitterness.
Simmer a few more minutes until the sauce lightly coats the bitter gourd.
Serve hot.

name: Tortang Talong
steps: Grill or roast the eggplant whole over a flame or under a broiler, turning occasionally, until the skin is charred and the flesh is soft.
Let cool slightly, then peel off the charred skin, keeping the stem intact, and flatten the flesh gently with a fork.
Beat the egg with salt and pepper in a shallow bowl.
Dip the flattened eggplant into the beaten egg, coating it well.
Heat cooking oil in a pan and fry the egg-coated eggplant until golden on both sides and the egg is fully set, with no runny egg remaining.
Drain briefly and serve hot.

name: Ginataang Kalabasa
steps: In a pot over medium heat, cook the pork belly until it releases some of its own fat, then add the onion, garlic and ginger and sauté until fragrant.
Stir in the bagoong alamang and season with the all-in-one seasoning.
Add the squash, cut into chunks, and enough water to keep things from sticking. Simmer until the squash and pork begin to soften.
Add the string beans and simmer until tender.
Stir in the coconut milk and simmer until the sauce thickens slightly.
The pork should be fully cooked through, with no pink remaining.

name: Ginisang Sayote
steps: Heat cooking oil in a pan and sauté the garlic, onion and tomato until softened.
Add the shrimp and cook until they turn pink and opaque.
Add the chayote, cut into strips, and stir-fry a minute.
Add the oyster sauce and a splash of water, and simmer until the chayote is just tender but still slightly crisp.
Season with salt and pepper.
Serve hot.

name: Ginisang Repolyo
steps: Heat cooking oil in a pan and sauté the garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the pork and cook until it changes color on the outside.
Pour in the beef broth and simmer until the pork is nearly tender.
Add the red bell pepper and cook a couple of minutes.
Add the cabbage last and cook just until wilted, still slightly crisp.
Season with salt and pepper. The pork should be fully cooked through, with no pink remaining.

name: Ginisang Upo
steps: Heat cooking oil in a pan and sauté the garlic, onion and tomato until softened.
Stir in the saute seasoning and add a splash of water.
Add the bottle gourd, cut into chunks, and simmer until tender, about 10 minutes.
Stir occasionally so it cooks evenly.
The bottle gourd should be soft enough to easily pierce with a fork.
Serve hot.

name: Ginataang Sitaw at Kalabasa
steps: Heat cooking oil in a pot and sauté the onion, garlic and ginger until fragrant.
Add the pork and cook until it changes color on the outside.
Add a pork cube dissolved in a little water, and the squash cut into chunks. Simmer until the squash and pork begin to soften.
Add the string beans and simmer until tender.
Stir in the coconut milk and simmer until the sauce thickens slightly.
Season with fish sauce and black pepper. The pork should be fully cooked through, with no pink remaining.

name: Adobong Sitaw
steps: Heat cooking oil in a pan and sauté the garlic and shallots until fragrant.
Add the pork and cook until it changes color on the outside.
Add the vinegar and simmer without stirring for a minute, to cook off its raw sharpness.
Stir in the oyster sauce and brown sugar, and simmer until the pork is nearly tender.
Add the string beans and cook until just tender but still bright green.
Season with black pepper. The pork should be fully cooked through, with no pink remaining.

name: Ginisang Togue
steps: Heat cooking oil in a pan and sauté the garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the shrimp and cook until they turn pink and opaque.
Add the carrot and green beans, and stir-fry a few minutes until they begin to soften.
Add the bean sprouts and stir-fry just until they wilt slightly but still have some crunch.
Season with fish sauce and salt.
Serve immediately while still crisp.

name: Dinengdeng
steps: In a pot, combine the onion, tomato and ginger with enough water to cover, and bring to a boil.
Stir in the fermented fish paste.
Add the squash, cut into chunks, and simmer until it begins to soften.
Add the milkfish and simmer until it's cooked through and flakes easily.
Add the string beans, okra and bitter gourd, and simmer until tender.
Add the moringa last and cook just until wilted. The milkfish should be opaque throughout, with no translucent center.

name: Utan Bisaya
steps: In a pot, combine the ginger and tomato with enough water to cover, and bring to a boil.
Add the squash, cut into chunks, and simmer until it begins to soften.
Add the fish and long green chili, and simmer until the fish is cooked through and flakes easily.
Add the eggplant, string beans, okra and sponge gourd, and simmer until tender.
Add the spinach and moringa last and cook just until wilted.
Season with salt, top with spring onion, and serve. The fish should be opaque throughout, with no translucent center.

name: Ensaladang Talong
steps: Grill or roast the eggplant and bitter gourd whole, turning occasionally, until softened and lightly charred.
Let cool slightly, then peel the eggplant and slice both vegetables into bite-sized pieces.
In a small pot, warm the coconut milk with the garlic, onion, tomato and ginger until fragrant, then season with the all-in-one seasoning.
Let the coconut milk mixture cool slightly, then pour it over the grilled vegetables and toss to coat.
Top with spring onion.
Serve at room temperature or chilled.

name: Atchara
steps: Grate or julienne the green papaya and carrot, then toss with salt and let sit for 30 minutes to draw out excess moisture.
Rinse the papaya and carrot well and squeeze out as much liquid as possible.
In a pot, combine the vinegar, sugar, ginger, onion and garlic, and bring to a boil, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Let the vinegar mixture cool slightly, then pack the papaya, carrot, red bell pepper and raisins into clean jars.
Pour the vinegar mixture over the vegetables, making sure they're fully submerged, and add black pepper.
Seal and refrigerate for at least a day before eating, to let the flavors develop.

name: Lumpiang Gulay
steps: Heat cooking oil in a pan and stir-fry the carrot until it begins to soften.
Add the left over lechon, chopped, and cook until warmed through.
Add the cabbage and bean sprouts, and stir-fry just until they wilt slightly but still have some crunch. Season with the all-in-one seasoning.
Let the filling cool slightly, then spoon portions onto the lumpia wrapper and roll tightly, tucking in the sides.
Heat cooking oil in a pan and fry the rolls until golden and crisp on all sides.
Drain briefly and serve with the lechon sauce for dipping.

name: Dinakdakan
steps: Place the pork in a pot with the bay leaf, salt and enough water to cover. Boil until tender, about 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Remove the pork, let cool, then grill it over charcoal or in a hot pan until lightly charred, then chop into small pieces.
Separately, boil the pork liver until just cooked through, with no pink remaining, then chop finely.
Boil the pig brain until fully cooked and firm, then mash it to use as a creamy binder.
In a bowl, combine the chopped pork, liver, mashed pig brain, onion, ginger and bird's eye chili.
Season with salt and pepper, and finish with a squeeze of calamansi. All the meat should be fully cooked through, with no pink or rawness remaining.

name: Ginisang Labanos
steps: Heat cooking oil in a pan and sauté the garlic, onion and tomato until softened.
Add the pork and cook until it changes color on the outside.
Add a splash of water and simmer until the pork is nearly tender.
Add the radish and carrot, and simmer until they begin to soften.
Add the shrimp and cook until they turn pink and opaque.
Season with fish sauce and black pepper. The pork should be fully cooked through, with no pink remaining.

name: Pancit Canton
steps: Heat cooking oil in a wok and sauté the garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the pork shoulder and chicken breast, sliced thin, and cook until the pork has no pink left and the chicken reaches 74°C (165°F) at the thickest pieces.
Add the chinese sausage and fish, and cook a couple of minutes more.
Pour in the chicken broth, add the soy sauce and oyster sauce, and bring to a boil.
Add the carrot, celery and napa cabbage, and simmer until they begin to soften.

Add the egg noodles, shrimp and snow peas, and toss until the noodles absorb the liquid and the shrimp turn pink and opaque. Season with salt and pepper. Check that the chicken reaches 74°C (165°F) and the pork reaches 63°C (145°F) before serving.

name: Pancit Bihon
steps: Soak the rice noodles in warm water until pliable, then drain.
Heat cooking oil in a wok and sauté the garlic and onion until fragrant.
Stir in the saute seasoning and oyster sauce, and add a splash of water.
Add the carrot and cook a couple of minutes, then add the cabbage and cook until it starts to wilt.
Add the drained rice noodles and toss well, letting them absorb the sauce until tender.
Season with black pepper, top with spring onion, and serve with calamansi on the side.

name: Pancit Palabok
steps: Heat cooking oil in a pot and sauté the garlic until fragrant.
Add the annatto seeds briefly to color the oil, then remove them and add the pork belly. Cook until it changes color on the outside.
Add the shrimp cube dissolved in enough water, and simmer until the pork is tender.
Whisk the flour and cornstarch with a little water into a slurry, then stir it into the simmering liquid and cook until it thickens into a smooth, orange sauce.
Season with salt and pepper. Fry the firm tofu in cooking oil until golden, then cut into small cubes.

Arrange the rice noodles on a platter, pour the sauce generously over them, and top with the shrimp, smoked fish, pork cracklings, fried tofu, sliced hard-boiled egg and spring onion. Serve with calamansi on the side.

name: Pancit Malabon
steps: Heat cooking oil in a pot and sauté the garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the pork belly and cook until it changes color on the outside.
Add the annatto seeds for color, then add enough water to cover and simmer until the pork is tender.
Add the shrimp and squid, and simmer just until the shrimp turn pink and opaque and the squid turns opaque. Do not overcook the squid, or it turns rubbery.
Add the napa cabbage and cook just until wilted. Season with fish sauce and black pepper.

Boil the rice noodles separately until tender, then drain and arrange on a platter. Pour the sauce and toppings over the noodles, and finish with the smoked fish, pork cracklings, sliced hard-boiled egg, parsley and a squeeze of lemon.

name: Pancit Habhab
