steps: Warm cooking oil in a wok, then soften the garlic and onion in it until fragrant.
Drop in the pork belly and let it cook until no longer pink on the outside.
Pour in the beef broth along with the soy sauce and oyster sauce, and let it simmer until the pork is nearly done.
Stir in the chayote and carrot, cooking until they start to give.

Add the fresh egg noodles, shrimp, snow peas and cabbage all at once, tossing everything together so the noodles soak up the sauce, the pork is fully cooked with no pink, and the shrimp turn pink and opaque.
Finish with black pepper and a splash of vinegar right before plating.

name: Pancit Sotanghon
steps: Heat cooking oil in a wok and sauté the garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the chicken and pork, sliced thin, and cook until they change color on the outside.
Add the chinese sausage and soy sauce, and cook a couple of minutes more.
Add enough water to cover, bring to a boil, and simmer until the chicken and pork are cooked through.
Add the carrot, green peas and cabbage, and simmer until they begin to soften.
Add the glass noodles and toss until they absorb the liquid and turn tender. Season with salt and pepper and top with parsley. Chicken should reach 74°C (165°F).

name: Lomi

ingredients.item: lomi noodles blanched and rinse well
ingredients.label: lomi noodles blanched and rinse well

steps: Heat cooking oil in a pot and sauté the garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the pork belly and cook until it changes color on the outside.
Add enough water to cover, season with the all-in-one seasoning and oyster sauce, and simmer until the pork is nearly tender.
Add the carrot and simmer until it softens.
Add the lomi noodles and stir well. Whisk the cornstarch with a little water into a slurry and stir it in to thicken the liquid.

Crack the egg into the simmering pot and stir it through until fully set, with no runny egg remaining. Add the napa cabbage and cook just until wilted. Top with spring onion and serve with calamansi on the side.

name: Chicken Mami
steps: In a pot, toast the garlic briefly until fragrant, then pour in the chicken broth and bring to a boil.
Add the chicken breast and simmer until cooked through.
Remove the chicken, let cool slightly, then shred or slice it, and return it to the pot.
Add the carrot and simmer until it softens.
Cook the egg noodles separately in boiling water until tender, then divide into bowls.

Ladle the hot chicken broth, chicken and carrot over the noodles. Add the napa cabbage and let it wilt in the hot liquid. Season with salt, and top with sliced hard-boiled egg and spring onion. Chicken should reach 74°C (165°F).

name: Bringhe
steps: Heat cooking oil in a pot and sauté the garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the chorizo and chicken thighs, and cook until the chicken changes color on the outside.
Stir in the turmeric, then add the glutinous rice and toast briefly to coat it in the color.
Pour in the coconut milk and chicken broth, season with fish sauce, and bring to a boil.
Lower the heat, cover, and simmer until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed, stirring occasionally so it doesn't stick.

Stir in the carrot, red bell pepper, green bell pepper, green peas and raisins, and cook a few more minutes. Season with salt and pepper, and top with sliced hard-boiled egg and banana. Chicken should reach 74°C (165°F).

name: Paella Filipina
steps: Heat olive oil in a wide pan and season the chicken with paprika and salt and pepper, then brown it on all sides. Set aside.
In the same pan, add the chorizo, garlic and onion, and sauté until fragrant.
Stir in the tomato sauce and rice, coating the rice in the sauce.
Dissolve the saffron in a little warm water and add it, along with enough water to cover the rice generously.
Return the chicken to the pan, bring to a simmer, and cook without stirring until the rice is nearly tender and most of the liquid is absorbed.
Nestle the mussels and shrimp into the rice and cook until the mussel shells open and the shrimp turn pink and opaque; discard any mussels that stay closed. Chicken should reach 74°C (165°F).

name: Sinangag
steps: Heat cooking oil in a pan or wok and fry the garlic until golden and crisp. Remove the garlic and set aside, keeping the garlic-infused oil in the pan.
Add the rice, breaking up any clumps, and stir-fry over high heat until heated through and slightly crisp in spots.
Season with salt.
Drizzle with sesame oil and toss to coat.
Stir in the chives just before removing from the heat.
Top with the fried garlic and serve hot.

name: Java Rice
steps: Heat cooking oil and butter in a pan and sauté the shallots and garlic until fragrant.
Add the annatto seeds briefly to color the oil, then remove them.
Stir in the turmeric and red bell pepper, and cook a minute.
Add the rice, breaking up any clumps, and stir-fry until heated through and evenly colored.
Season with soy sauce and salt and pepper.
Serve hot.

name: Arroz a la Valenciana
steps: Heat olive oil in a pot and sauté the garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the chicken thighs and chorizo, and cook until the chicken changes color on the outside.
Stir in the tomato paste, tomato and paprika, and cook a couple of minutes.
Dissolve the saffron in a little warm water, then add it along with the glutinous rice and rice, coating the grains in the sauce.
Pour in the chicken broth and coconut milk, bring to a boil, then lower the heat, cover, and simmer until the rice is tender, stirring occasionally so it doesn't stick.
Stir in the red bell pepper, raisins and green peas, and cook a few more minutes. Season with salt and pepper, and top with sliced hard-boiled egg. Chicken should reach 74°C (165°F).

name: Pancit Luglug
steps: Heat cooking oil in a pot and sauté the garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the pork and cook until it changes color on the outside.
Add the annatto seeds for color, then add enough water to cover and simmer until the pork is tender.
Whisk the flour and cornstarch with a little water into a slurry, then stir it into the simmering liquid and cook until it thickens into a smooth sauce.
Season with fish sauce and salt. Add the shrimp and simmer just until they turn pink and opaque.
Arrange the rice noodles on a platter, pour the sauce over them, and top with pork cracklings, sliced hard-boiled egg, garlic and spring onion. Serve with calamansi on the side.

name: Pancit Bam-i
steps: Heat cooking oil in a wok and sauté the garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the pork and chicken, sliced thin, and cook until they change color on the outside.
Add the chinese sausage, then pour in the chicken broth and add a chicken cube. Season with soy sauce and bring to a boil.
Add the carrot and wood ear mushroom, and simmer until they begin to soften.
Add the cabbage and shrimp, and simmer until the shrimp turn pink and opaque.
Add both the egg noodles and rice noodles, and toss until they absorb the liquid and turn tender. Season with salt, top with parsley, and serve. Chicken should reach 74°C (165°F).

name: Filipino Spaghetti
steps: Cook the spaghetti in a pot of boiling water until tender, then drain.
Heat cooking oil in a pan and sauté the garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the luncheon meat and hotdog, sliced, and cook until lightly browned.
Pour in the beef broth and simmer until slightly reduced.
Add the drained spaghetti and toss well, letting it absorb the sauce.
Season with salt and pepper, and top with grated cheese before serving.

name: Baked Macaroni
steps: Cook the macaroni in a pot of boiling water until just tender, then drain.
Heat cooking oil in a pan and sauté the garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the beef and hotdog, sliced, and cook until the beef changes color on the outside.

Stir in the tomato sauce, tomato paste and banana ketchup, along with the beef broth, sugar and italian seasoning. Add the green bell pepper and red bell pepper, and simmer until slightly thickened. Season with salt and pepper.

In a separate pot, melt the butter, whisk in the flour, and cook briefly, then gradually whisk in the milk until smooth and thickened. Season with nutmeg and salt and pepper, and stir in some of the cheese until melted.

Combine the macaroni with the meat sauce in a baking dish, pour the cheese sauce over the top, sprinkle with the remaining cheese, and bake until bubbly and golden on top, 20–25 minutes. Beef should be fully cooked through, with no pink remaining.

name: Pancit Lomi Batangas
steps: Heat cooking oil in a pot and sauté the garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the beef and cook until it changes color on the outside.
Add a beef cube dissolved in enough water to cover, season with soy sauce, and simmer until the beef is tender.
Add the carrot and simmer until it softens.
Whisk the flour and cornstarch with a little water into a slurry, then stir it into the simmering liquid and cook until it thickens.

Add the fresh noodles and stir well. Crack the egg into the pot and stir it through until fully set, with no runny egg remaining. Season with salt, and top with spring onion, sliced hard-boiled egg and pork cracklings.

name: Bibingkang Malagkit
steps: Rinse the glutinous rice and place it in a pot with the pandan leaf and enough water to cover. Cook until the rice is tender and the water is absorbed.
Stir in the coconut milk, sugar and salt, and cook over low heat, stirring often, until the mixture thickens and turns sticky.
Remove the pandan leaf. Spread the mixture into a greased baking dish.
Top with grated coconut and sprinkle brown sugar evenly over the surface.
Bake or broil until the top is lightly caramelized and golden in spots, watching closely so the sugar doesn't burn.
Let cool slightly before slicing and serving.

name: Champorado
steps: Rinse the glutinous rice and place it in a pot with enough water to cover generously. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer, stirring occasionally so it doesn't stick.
Once the rice starts to soften and thicken, stir in the cocoa and sugar.
Continue simmering, stirring often, until the rice is fully tender and the mixture is thick and porridge-like.
Adjust with a little more water if it gets too thick.
Ladle into bowls and drizzle generously with evaporated milk.
Serve warm.

name: Miki Bihon
steps: Heat cooking oil in a pot and sauté the garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the chicken thighs and cook until it changes color on the outside.
Pour in the chicken broth, season with the sweet soy sauce, and simmer until the chicken is nearly cooked through.
Add the fish and carrot, and simmer until the fish flakes easily and the carrot softens.
Add the shrimp, fresh egg noodles and rice noodles, and simmer until the shrimp turn pink and opaque and the noodles are tender.
Add the napa cabbage and cook just until wilted. Season with salt and pepper, top with spring onion, and serve with calamansi on the side. Chicken should reach 74°C (165°F).

name: Pancit Cabagan
steps: Heat cooking oil in a pot and sauté the garlic until fragrant.
Add the pork shoulder and cook until it changes color on the outside.
Pour in the beef broth, season with soy sauce and fish sauce, and simmer until the pork is tender.
Add the carrot and green bell pepper, and simmer until they soften.
Add the fresh egg noodles and cabbage, and toss until the noodles absorb the liquid and are tender.
Season with black pepper, top with parsley, spring onion, quail eggs, the cooked lechon carajay and igado. Pork should be fully cooked through, with no pink remaining.

name: Lumpiang Shanghai
steps: In a bowl, mix the pork with the onion and carrot, both finely chopped, and season with the all-in-one seasoning.
Spoon a portion of the filling onto a lumpia wrapper and roll tightly into a thin cylinder, sealing the edge with a little water.
Repeat with the remaining filling and wrappers.
Heat cooking oil in a pan for deep-frying.
Fry the rolls in batches until golden brown and crisp on all sides, and the ground-pork filling reaches 71°C (160°F) with no pink remaining.
Drain briefly on paper towels before serving.

name: Lumpiang Sariwa
steps: Heat cooking oil in a pan and sauté the garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the sweet potato and carrot, cut into thin strips, and stir-fry until they begin to soften.
Add the green beans and bean sprouts, season with fish sauce and sugar, and cook until the vegetables are just tender.
Beat the egg with a pinch of salt and cook into a thin sheet in a lightly oiled pan, then slice into thin strips.

For the sauce, combine soy sauce, brown sugar and a little water in a small pot, bring to a simmer, then stir in the peanut butter and crushed peanuts. Thicken with a cornstarch slurry and add a touch of garlic and salt.
Wrap the vegetable filling in the egg crepe, top with lettuce, and drizzle generously with the peanut sauce before serving.

name: Tokwa't Baboy
steps: Place the pork and pork belly in a pot with the bay leaf, salt and enough water to cover. Boil until tender, about 45 minutes.
Remove and let cool, then chop into small pieces.
Heat cooking oil in a pan and fry the firm tofu, cut into cubes, until golden on all sides.
In a bowl, combine the vinegar, soy sauce, sugar, shallots, garlic and bird's eye chili to make the dipping sauce.
Toss the chopped pork and fried tofu together, then season with black pepper.
Pour the sauce over just before serving, or serve it on the side. The pork should be fully cooked through, with no pink remaining.

name: Kwek-Kwek
steps: Boil the quail eggs until fully cooked through, then peel.
In a bowl, whisk together the flour, cornstarch, baking powder, salt, black pepper, food coloring and the all-in-one seasoning with enough water to make a thick batter.
Heat cooking oil in a pan for deep-frying.
Dip the peeled quail eggs into the batter, coating them fully, and fry until the coating is crisp and deep orange, a couple of minutes.
For the dipping sauce, combine the vinegar, banana ketchup, brown sugar, soy sauce, garlic, shallots and bird's eye chili in a small bowl.
Drain the fried eggs briefly and serve hot with the dipping sauce.

name: Okoy
steps: In a bowl, whisk together the flour, egg and enough water to make a batter, and season with the all-in-one seasoning and black pepper.
Stir in the green papaya, cut into thin strips, and the bean sprouts.
Heat cooking oil in a pan for shallow-frying.
Scoop portions of the batter into the hot oil, pressing a few shrimp on top of each, and fry until golden and crisp on both sides.
For the dipping sauce, combine the vinegar, garlic, onion, sugar and soy sauce.
Drain briefly and serve hot with the dipping sauce. The shrimp should be pink and opaque throughout.

name: Chicharon
steps: Place the ruffle fat in a pot with the bay leaf and enough water to cover. Simmer until the fat is tender and most of the water has evaporated, about 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Remove and let cool completely, then air-dry, uncovered, until the surface is dry to the touch, ideally a few hours or overnight. A dry surface helps it puff when fried.
Heat cooking oil in a pot for deep-frying, over medium heat first.
Fry the dried fat slowly until it turns light golden and most of the moisture has cooked out.
Remove and let cool, then raise the oil to high heat and fry the pieces a second time, briefly, until they puff up and turn deep golden and crisp.
Drain well and toss with salt and black pepper while still hot.

name: Isaw
steps: Clean the small intestine thoroughly, turning it inside out and scrubbing well, then rinse repeatedly until the water runs clear.
Place it in a pot with the bay leaf, salt and enough water to cover. Boil until tender, about 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Drain and let cool, then thread onto skewers.
In a bowl, combine the soy sauce, vinegar, garlic, chinese cooking wine, sugar and black pepper to make a basting sauce.
Brush the skewers with cooking oil and the basting sauce, then grill over hot coals, basting and turning occasionally, until lightly charred.
Serve hot with a vinegar and bird's eye chili dipping sauce on the side. The intestine should be tender throughout, with no rawness.

name: Turon
steps: Slice the banana lengthwise and place a strip of jackfruit alongside it on a lumpia wrapper.
Sprinkle sugar over the banana and jackfruit.
Roll the wrapper tightly around the filling, sealing the edge with a little water.
Heat cooking oil in a pan.
Fry the rolls, turning occasionally, until the wrapper is golden and the sugar caramelizes into a crisp, sticky shell.
Drain briefly and let cool slightly before serving, as the caramelized sugar stays very hot.

name: Banana Cue
steps: Heat cooking oil in a pan.
Add the banana, whole or halved, and fry until it starts to turn golden.
Sprinkle brown sugar over the banana in the pan.
Continue frying, turning occasionally, until the brown sugar melts and caramelizes into a sticky coating on all sides.
Skewer the bananas while still warm.
Let cool slightly before serving, as the caramelized coating stays very hot.

name: Camote Cue
steps: Slice the sweet potato into rounds or wedges.
Heat cooking oil in a pan and fry the sweet potato until it softens and starts to turn golden.
Sprinkle brown sugar over the sweet potato in the pan.
Continue frying, turning occasionally, until the brown sugar melts and caramelizes into a sticky coating on all sides.
Skewer the pieces while still warm.
Let cool slightly before serving, as the caramelized coating stays very hot.

name: Dynamite Lumpia
steps: Slit the bird's eye chili lengthwise, keeping the stem intact, and scrape out some of the seeds to make room for the filling.
In a bowl, mix the pork with the garlic and spring onion, finely chopped, and season with salt and black pepper.
Stuff each chili with a portion of the pork filling.
Wrap each stuffed chili in a lumpia wrapper, rolling tightly and sealing the edge with a little water.
Heat cooking oil in a pan and fry the rolls until golden and crisp on all sides, and the ground-pork filling reaches 71°C (160°F) with no pink remaining.
Drain briefly before serving.

name: Cheese Sticks
steps: Cut the cheese into thin sticks.
Wrap each stick of cheese in a lumpia wrapper, rolling tightly and sealing the edge with a little water.
Heat cooking oil in a pan.
Fry the rolls in batches until golden and crisp on all sides.
Work quickly once the cheese starts to melt, since overcooked rolls can burst.
Drain briefly and serve hot while the cheese is still soft inside.

name: Empanada
steps: For the dough, combine the flour, sugar and salt, then cut in the butter until crumbly. Add the egg and enough milk to bring it together into a smooth dough. Wrap and chill while you make the filling.
Heat cooking oil in a pan and sauté the garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the beef and cook until it changes color on the outside.
Add the potato and carrot, cut into small cubes, and the tomato sauce, and simmer until the vegetables are tender and the beef is fully cooked through.
Stir in the green peas and raisins, and season with salt and pepper. Let the filling cool.
Roll out the dough, cut into rounds, fill with the beef mixture, fold over and crimp the edges. Fry in cooking oil until golden, or bake until golden brown.

name: Siomai
steps: In a bowl, combine the pork and shrimp, chopped, with the mushroom and water chestnut, finely chopped.
Add the spring onion, ginger, cornstarch, sesame oil, chinese cooking wine, soy sauce, salt, black pepper, sugar and a crumbled chicken cube, and mix well.
Spoon a portion of the filling onto a wonton wrapper and gather the edges up around it, leaving the top open, pressing gently to shape.
Arrange the dumplings in a steamer lined with parchment paper so they don't stick.
Steam until the filling reaches 71°C (160°F), with no pink remaining, about 15–20 minutes.
Serve with a dipping sauce of soy sauce, garlic and calamansi.

name: Siopao
steps: For the dough, dissolve the yeast and a little sugar in warm milk, then mix with the flour, baking powder, salt and cooking oil into a smooth dough. Cover and let rise until doubled, about 1 hour.
Meanwhile, heat cooking oil in a pot and sauté the garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the pork shoulder and cook until it changes color on the outside.
Add the soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar and star anise, along with enough water to cover, and simmer until the pork is very tender.
Shred the pork, thicken the sauce with a cornstarch slurry, and let the filling cool.

Punch down the dough, divide into portions, flatten and fill with the pork mixture, then gather and seal. Steam until the buns are puffed and cooked through, about 15–20 minutes. The pork should be fully cooked through, with no pink remaining.

name: Fish Ball
steps: In a food processor or by hand, blend the fish into a smooth paste with the onion and spring onion.
Mix in the tapioca starch, salt and black pepper until the mixture holds together.
Shape the mixture into small balls.
Bring the vegetable broth to a boil in a pot, then drop in the fish balls and cook until they float and are fully cooked through, about 5–8 minutes.
Remove the boiled balls and deep-fry them until golden for a crisp street-food crust.
Add the bok choy to the remaining vegetable broth and simmer just until wilted. Season with fish sauce, and serve the balls with the vegetable broth or a dipping sauce.

name: Food for the Gods
steps: Preheat the oven and grease a baking pan.
Cream the butter with the brown sugar and sugar until light and fluffy, then beat in the egg, honey and vanilla.
Stir in the all purpose cream.
In a separate bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder and salt, then fold into the wet mixture.
Fold in the raisins and chopped cashew.
Pour into the prepared pan and bake until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean, about 25–30 minutes. Let cool before slicing into bars.

name: Pianono
steps: Preheat the oven and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Beat the eggs with the cream of tartar until foamy, then gradually beat in the sugar until thick, pale and tripled in volume.
Whisk in the milk and vanilla, then gently fold in the flour, cornstarch and baking powder, being careful not to deflate the batter.
Spread the batter evenly onto the prepared sheet and bake until springy to the touch, about 12–15 minutes.
While still warm, roll the cake up with a sugar-dusted cloth and let it cool in that shape. Unroll, spread with a filling of creamed butter and powdered sugar, and roll back up before slicing.

name: Tokneneng
steps: Peel the hard-boiled egg.
In a bowl, whisk together the flour, cornstarch, annatto, salt and black pepper with enough water to make a thick batter, until it turns a deep orange color.
Heat cooking oil in a pan for deep-frying.
Dip the peeled eggs into the batter, coating them fully.
Fry until the coating is crisp and deep orange, a couple of minutes.
Drain briefly and serve hot.

name: Maruya
steps: In a bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder and salt.
Whisk in the egg, milk and melted butter until you have a smooth batter.
Slice the banana thinly lengthwise and dip the slices into the batter, coating them well.
Heat cooking oil in a pan for shallow-frying.
Fry the battered banana slices until golden brown and crisp on both sides.
Drain briefly, dust with extra sugar, and serve hot.

name: Ginataang Bilo-Bilo
steps: Combine the rice flour with a little water to form a soft dough, then roll into small balls.
In a pot, bring the coconut milk to a gentle simmer with the sugar.
Add the tapioca pearls and simmer until they turn translucent.
Drop in the rice flour balls and simmer until they float and are cooked through.
Add the jackfruit and simmer a few more minutes.
Stir in the coconut cream last, off the heat, so it doesn't separate, and serve warm.

name: Lumpiang Ubod
steps: Heat cooking oil in a pan and sauté the garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add the pork and cook until no pink remains, then add the shrimp cube dissolved in a little water.
Add the heart of palm, cut into thin strips, and the carrot, and cook until tender. Add the shrimp and cook until pink and opaque. Season with fish sauce and stir in the parsley.
For the wrapper, whisk the flour and egg with water into a thin batter, and cook into thin crepes in a lightly oiled pan.
For the sauce, combine soy sauce, brown sugar and a little water in a small pot, bring to a simmer, and thicken with a cornstarch slurry; stir in a little garlic.
Wrap the vegetable filling in the crepe, top with lettuce and crushed peanuts, and drizzle with the sauce before serving.

name: Pinaputok na Tilapia
steps: Clean the tilapia and season it inside and out with salt and pepper.
Stuff the cavity with the tomato, onion, ginger and garlic.
Rub the tamarind over the fish, and dot with butter.
Wrap the fish tightly in foil.
Grill or bake the wrapped fish until the flesh is opaque throughout and flakes easily, about 20–25 minutes.
Unwrap carefully, drizzle with soy sauce and a squeeze of calamansi, and serve hot.

name: Lechon Manok
steps: In a bowl, combine the fish sauce, soy sauce, brown sugar, garlic, shallots and a squeeze of calamansi to make a marinade.
Rub the chicken all over, inside and out, with salt and pepper, then stuff the cavity with the lemongrass.
Pour the marinade over the chicken and let it marinate, refrigerated, for at least a few hours or overnight.
Skewer the chicken on a rotisserie spit, or place it on a rack.
Roast over charcoal or in an oven, turning occasionally, until the skin is deeply browned and crisp.
The chicken should reach 74°C (165°F) at the thickest part, with no pink near the bone. Rest briefly before carving.

name: Inihaw na Liempo
steps: In a bowl, combine the liquid seasoning, soy sauce, banana ketchup, calamansi, black pepper and garlic to make a marinade.
Marinate the pork belly in the mixture, refrigerated, for at least a few hours or overnight.
Reserve some of the marinade for basting, keeping it separate from what touched the raw pork.
Brush the grill with cooking oil, then grill the pork belly over hot coals, basting occasionally with the reserved marinade.
Turn occasionally and grill until the pork reaches 63°C (145°F), then rest briefly; it should show no pink and be nicely charred at the edges.
Squeeze lemon over the top before serving.

name: Pork Barbecue
steps: Slice the pork belly into thin strips.
In a bowl, combine the soy sauce, banana ketchup, liquid seasoning, garlic powder, calamansi and black pepper to make a marinade.
Marinate the pork in the mixture, refrigerated, for at least a few hours or overnight.
Thread the marinated pork onto skewers.
Reserve some of the marinade for basting, keeping it separate from what touched the raw pork, then grill the skewers over hot coals, basting and turning occasionally.
Grill until the pork reaches 63°C (145°F), then rest briefly; it should show no pink and be lightly charred at the edges.

name: Leche Flan
steps: In a llanera or shallow pan, melt the sugar over low heat until it turns into a deep amber caramel, then swirl to coat the bottom evenly. Set aside to harden.
In a bowl, whisk the egg gently, avoiding too much foam, with the condensed milk, evaporated milk and vanilla until smooth.
Strain the mixture through a fine sieve into the caramel-lined pan, to keep the top perfectly smooth.
Cover tightly with foil.
Steam over gently simmering water until just set. The center should jiggle slightly but not look liquid, about 30–40 minutes.
Let cool, then chill before unmolding onto a plate so the caramel runs down the sides.

name: Halo-Halo
steps: Prepare the agar-agar according to its package, setting it into a firm gel, then cut into small cubes.
In a tall glass, layer the sweetened beans, nata de coco, sugar palm fruit, jackfruit, macapuno and cubed agar-agar.
Add sliced banana, purple yam and mango on top.
Fill the glass with shaved or crushed ice.
Pour the evaporated milk generously over the ice.
Top with a slice of leche flan and serve immediately with a long spoon, mixing everything together before eating.

name: Bibingka
steps: In a bowl, whisk together the rice flour, sugar, baking powder and salt.
Whisk in the coconut milk and egg until you have a smooth batter.
Pour the batter into a greased pan, and top with slices of salted egg and cheese.
Bake or cook over coals, top and bottom, until the center is set and a toothpick comes out clean, about 20–25 minutes.
Brush the top with butter and sprinkle with sugar while still hot.
Top with grated coconut and serve warm.

name: Puto Bumbong
steps: Soak the rice in water for at least a few hours, or overnight, until softened.
Drain and grind the rice into a fine, slightly wet meal.
Pack the ground rice into traditional bumbong tubes, or a similar steaming mold.
Steam until the rice is fully cooked through and holds its shape, about 15–20 minutes.
Unmold while still hot.
Brush with butter, sprinkle generously with brown sugar, and top with grated coconut before serving.

name: Puto
steps: In a bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar and baking powder.
Whisk in the egg, evaporated milk, melted butter and vanilla until smooth.
Pour the batter into small greased molds, filling them about three-quarters full.
Top each with a slice of cheese.
Steam until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean, about 15–20 minutes.
Let cool slightly before unmolding and serving.

name: Kutsinta
steps: In a bowl, whisk together the flour, tapioca starch and brown sugar.
Whisk in enough water to make a smooth batter, then stir in the annatto for color and a small amount of lye water for the chewy texture.
Pour the batter into small greased molds.
Steam until the mixture turns translucent and sets firm, about 20–25 minutes.
Let cool slightly before unmolding.
Serve on its own, or alongside other kakanin, once fully cooled.

name: Sapin-Sapin
steps: In a bowl, whisk together the rice flour, coconut milk, condensed milk and sugar until smooth; divide the batter into portions for as many layers as you'd like.
Mix mashed purple yam into one portion and chopped jackfruit into another, leaving one plain, to give each layer a different flavor and color.
Pour the first layer into a greased steaming pan and steam until just set, about 10 minutes.
Pour the next layer on top and steam again until set. Repeat with the remaining layers.
Once all layers are steamed through, brush the top with coconut cream.
Let cool before slicing and serving.

name: Biko
steps: Rinse the glutinous rice and steam or boil it until just tender.
In a pot, combine the coconut milk, brown sugar and salt, and bring to a simmer, stirring until the brown sugar dissolves.
Add the cooked rice to the pot and stir well, cooking over low heat until the mixture thickens and turns sticky, and most of the liquid is absorbed.
Spread the mixture into a greased pan and press down evenly.
Drizzle the coconut cream over the top and let it caramelize slightly under a broiler, or spread it on as a topping without broiling.
Let cool before slicing and serving.

name: Maja Blanca
steps: In a pot, combine the coconut milk, corn and sugar, and bring to a simmer.
Whisk the cornstarch with a little water into a slurry.
Gradually stir the slurry into the simmering coconut milk, cooking and stirring constantly until it thickens into a smooth, pudding-like consistency.
Pour into a greased pan and spread evenly.
Let cool to room temperature, then chill until fully set.
Top with grated coconut before slicing and serving.

name: Buko Pandan
steps: Prepare the agar-agar with sugar according to its package, then let it set into a firm gel.
Once set, cut the gel into small cubes or thin strips.
In a large bowl, combine the agar-agar, grated coconut, all purpose cream and condensed milk.
Stir gently to combine everything evenly.
Chill for at least an hour before serving.
Serve cold.

name: Ube Halaya
steps: Boil or steam the purple yam until very tender, then mash it smooth.
In a wide pan, combine the mashed purple yam with the coconut milk, condensed milk, evaporated milk, sugar and ube extract.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until the mixture thickens and pulls away from the sides of the pan, 30–40 minutes. Keep stirring to avoid scorching.
Stir in the butter a little at a time until fully incorporated and glossy.
Fold in grated cheese for a salty contrast.
Spread into a dish, top with coconut cream, and let cool before serving.

name: Brazo de Mercedes
steps: For the filling, whisk the egg yolk with the condensed milk and vanilla in a pot over low heat, stirring constantly, until thickened. Stir in a little calamansi juice for brightness, then let cool.
Preheat the oven and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Beat the egg white with the cream of tartar until soft peaks form, then gradually beat in the sugar until stiff and glossy.
Spread the meringue evenly onto the prepared sheet and bake until lightly golden on top, about 12–15 minutes.
While still warm, spread the cooled custard filling over the meringue and roll it up carefully using the parchment to guide it.
Dust with powdered sugar before slicing and serving.

name: Sans Rival
steps: Preheat the oven and line baking sheets with parchment.
Beat the egg white with the cream of tartar until soft peaks form, then gradually beat in half the sugar until stiff and glossy. Fold in the chopped cashew.
Spread the meringue into thin, even layers on the parchment and bake until dry and lightly golden, about 20–25 minutes. Let cool completely.
For the buttercream, whisk the egg yolk with the remaining sugar and vanilla over low heat, stirring constantly, until thickened, then let cool.
Beat the cooled yolk mixture into the butter, a little at a time, until light and fluffy.
Layer the cooled meringue sheets with the buttercream in between, then coat the outside with more buttercream and press chopped cashew onto the sides.

name: Ensaymada
steps: Dissolve the yeast and a little sugar in warm milk, and let sit until foamy.
In a large bowl, combine the flour, remaining sugar and salt, then mix in the egg, the yeast mixture and some of the butter to form a soft dough. Knead until smooth and elastic.
Cover and let rise until doubled, about 1 to 1.5 hours.
Punch down the dough, divide into portions, and shape each into a coil, working in some of the remaining butter as you shape it.
Place on a baking sheet, cover, and let rise again until puffy.
Bake until golden, then brush generously with butter and top with sugar and grated cheese while still warm.

name: Yema
steps: In a pot, combine the egg yolk, condensed milk and a splash of vinegar. The vinegar keeps the mixture from curdling as it cooks.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until the mixture thickens into a soft, pliable dough, 10–15 minutes.
Let cool until safe to handle.
Roll the mixture into small balls.
Roll each ball in sugar to coat.
Wrap individually in candy wrappers or cellophane, twisting the ends, and let set before serving.

name: Pastillas de Leche
steps: In a pan, combine the condensed milk and milk, and cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until the mixture thickens into a soft dough that pulls away from the pan.
Let cool until safe to handle.
Dust a work surface with sugar and roll the mixture into small logs.
Roll each log in sugar to coat evenly.
Wrap individually in candy wrappers or cellophane, twisting the ends.
Let set before serving.

name: Polvoron
steps: Toast the flour in a dry pan over low heat, stirring constantly, until lightly golden and fragrant. Let cool.
Toast the pounded young rice separately in the same way, then let cool.
In a bowl, combine the toasted flour, toasted pounded young rice, sugar, chopped cashew and crushed oreo cookies.
Melt the butter and mix it into the dry ingredients until evenly moistened and crumbly.
Pack the mixture firmly into a polvoron mold, then unmold onto a tray.
Wrap individually in paper, twisting the ends, and let set before serving.

name: Cassava Cake
steps: Grate the cassava and squeeze out excess liquid.
In a bowl, combine the grated cassava with the coconut milk, condensed milk, sugar, melted butter and macapuno, and mix well.
Pour into a greased baking pan and bake until mostly set, about 30–35 minutes.
Meanwhile, boil or steam the purple yam until tender, then mash it with the evaporated milk, condensed milk, sugar, butter and ube extract until smooth.
Spread the purple yam mixture over the partially baked cassava layer, then top with grated cheese.
Return to the oven and bake until fully set and the top is golden, another 20–25 minutes. Let cool before slicing.

name: Pichi-Pichi
steps: Grate the cassava and squeeze out excess liquid.
In a bowl, combine the grated cassava with sugar, salt, a small amount of lye water, food coloring and chopped pandan, and mix well.
Pour the mixture into small greased molds.
Steam until the mixture turns translucent and sets firm, about 25–30 minutes.
Let cool slightly before unmolding.
Roll each piece in grated coconut, then top with grated cheese.

name: Palitaw
steps: Combine the rice flour with enough water to form a soft, pliable dough.
Pinch off small portions and flatten them into thin discs.
Drop the discs into a pot of boiling water and cook until they float to the surface, a couple of minutes.
Remove and drain, then roll each piece in grated coconut.
Sprinkle with sugar and toasted sesame seeds.
Serve warm or at room temperature.

name: Suman
steps: Grate the cassava and squeeze out excess liquid.
In a bowl, combine the grated cassava with the coconut milk and sugar, and mix well.
Spoon portions of the mixture onto foil, and wrap tightly into logs.
Steam the wrapped logs until firm and fully cooked through, about 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Let cool slightly before unwrapping.
Serve warm or at room temperature.

name: Ginataang Mais
steps: Rinse the glutinous rice and place it in a pot with enough water to cover generously. Simmer until it starts to soften.
Add the corn and coconut milk, and continue simmering, stirring occasionally so it doesn't stick.
Stir in the sugar and simmer until the rice is fully tender and the mixture thickens.
Stir in the coconut cream last, off the heat, so it doesn't separate.
The rice should be fully soft, with no hard bite left.
Serve warm.

name: Mango Float
steps: Whip the all purpose cream with the condensed milk until thick and well combined.
Slice the mango thinly.
In a dish, layer graham crackers, a spread of the cream mixture, and a layer of sliced mango.
Repeat the layers until you reach the top of the dish, finishing with a layer of cream.
Cover and chill for at least a few hours, or overnight, so the crackers soften.
Slice and serve cold.

name: Buko Salad
steps: Drain the fruit cocktail and canned pineapple well.
In a large bowl, combine the young coconut, sugar palm fruit, nata de coco, fruit cocktail and canned pineapple.
Add the condensed milk and all purpose cream, and mix gently until everything is well coated.
Chill for at least an hour before serving.
Stir gently before serving, since the fruit settles at the bottom.
Serve cold.

name: Filipino Fruit Salad
steps: Drain the fruit cocktail well.
Slice the strawberry and kiwi into bite-sized pieces.
In a large bowl, combine the fruit cocktail, strawberry, blueberry, kiwi and nata de coco.
Add the condensed milk and all purpose cream, and mix gently until everything is well coated.
Chill for at least an hour before serving.
Serve cold.

name: Taho
steps: In a pot, combine the brown sugar with the pandan and a little water, and simmer until it forms a light syrup. Remove the pandan.
Cook the tapioca pearls separately in boiling water until translucent and tender, then drain.
Gently steam or warm the silken tofu until heated through, being careful not to break it apart.
Scoop the warm silken tofu into a cup or bowl.
Top with the cooked tapioca pearls.
Drizzle generously with the brown sugar syrup and serve warm.

name: Tibok-Tibok
steps: In a bowl, whisk the rice flour with a little of the milk until smooth, to prevent lumps.
In a pot, combine the remaining milk, coconut cream and sugar, and bring to a simmer.
Gradually whisk in the rice flour mixture, stirring constantly, until it thickens into a smooth, pudding-like consistency.
Continue cooking over low heat, stirring, until no raw starch taste remains, a few more minutes.
Pour into a dish and spread evenly.
Let cool to room temperature, then chill until fully set before slicing.

name: Silvanas
steps: Preheat the oven and line baking sheets with parchment.
Beat the egg white with the cream of tartar until soft peaks form, then gradually beat in half the sugar until stiff and glossy. Fold in the flour and chopped cashew.
Spread the meringue into small, even rounds on the parchment and bake until dry and lightly golden, about 20–25 minutes. Let cool completely.
For the buttercream, whisk the egg yolk with the remaining sugar and vanilla over low heat, stirring constantly, until thickened, then let cool.
Beat the cooled yolk mixture into the butter, a little at a time, until light and fluffy.
Sandwich two meringue rounds together with the buttercream, coat the edges with more buttercream, and roll in crushed graham crackers and chopped cashew.

name: Mamon
steps: Preheat the oven and grease small mamon molds or a muffin tin.
Beat the egg with the cream of tartar until foamy, then gradually beat in the sugar until thick and pale.
Whisk in the milk, cooking oil and ube extract.
In a separate bowl, whisk together the flour and baking powder, then gently fold into the egg mixture, being careful not to deflate the batter.
Pour into the prepared molds, filling about two-thirds full.
Bake until the tops spring back to the touch and a thin skewer poked into the middle pulls out clean, about 15–18 minutes.

name: Pandesal
steps: Dissolve the yeast and a little sugar in warm milk, and let sit until foamy.
In a large bowl, combine the flour, remaining sugar and salt, then mix in the egg, melted butter and the yeast mixture to form a soft dough. Knead until smooth and elastic.
Cover and let rise until doubled, about 1 hour.
Punch down the dough, shape into a log, and cut into individual rolls.
Roll each piece in breadcrumbs, then place on a baking sheet and let rise again until puffy.
Bake until golden brown, about 15–18 minutes.

name: Nilupak
steps: Boil or steam the cassava until very tender.
Mash the cassava while still hot, with a pinch of salt, until smooth.
Mix in the condensed milk and butter until fully incorporated and glossy.
Spread the mixture onto a flat surface or dish, greased lightly, and press down evenly.
Top with grated cheese.
Let cool slightly before slicing and serving.

name: Espasol
steps: Toast some of the rice flour in a dry pan over low heat, stirring constantly, until lightly golden and fragrant. Set aside for coating.
In a pot, combine the remaining rice flour, coconut milk, sugar and vanilla, and cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until it thickens into a soft, sticky dough.
Let cool slightly until safe to handle.
Roll the dough into logs, then roll each log in the toasted rice flour to coat.
Roll again in grated coconut.
Slice into pieces and serve.

name: Egg Pie
steps: For the crust, combine the flour and salt, then cut in the butter until crumbly. Add enough cold water to bring it together into a dough. Roll out and fit into a pie pan.
In a bowl, whisk the egg and egg yolk with the sugar until smooth.
Whisk in the evaporated milk and vanilla.
Pour the filling into the prepared crust.
Bake until the edges are set but the center still jiggles slightly, about 30–35 minutes.
Let cool completely before slicing, as the filling continues to set as it cools.

name: Buko Pie
steps: For the crust, combine the flour and salt, then cut in the pork fat until crumbly. Add enough cold water and a squeeze of lemon to bring it together into a dough. Divide in two, and roll out one half to fit a pie pan.
In a pot, combine the young coconut, coconut, sugar, all purpose cream and milk, and bring to a gentle simmer.
Whisk the cornstarch with a little water into a slurry, then stir it into the simmering mixture and cook until thickened.
Let the filling cool slightly, then pour it into the prepared crust.
Roll out the second half of the dough and cover the pie, sealing and crimping the edges. Brush the top with beaten egg.
Bake until the crust is golden brown, about 30–35 minutes. Let cool before slicing.

name: Binatog
steps: Boil the corn kernels in water until tender, about 30–40 minutes.
Drain well and let cool slightly.
Toss the warm corn with grated coconut.
Add a little melted butter and toss again.
Sprinkle with sugar to taste.
Serve warm in small bowls or cups.

name: Crema de Fruta
steps: Preheat the oven and line a baking pan with parchment.
Beat the egg white with the cream of tartar until soft peaks form, then gradually beat in some of the sugar until stiff and glossy.

In a separate bowl, whisk the egg yolk with the remaining sugar, cooking oil and vanilla, then fold in the flour, baking powder and salt. Gently fold in the meringue, being careful not to deflate the batter.
Spread into the prepared pan and bake until springy to the touch, about 15–18 minutes. Let cool.

For the custard, whisk the egg yolk with the sugar and cornstarch, then gradually whisk in the milk. Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until thickened, then stir in the butter and vanilla. Let cool slightly, then spread over the cooled cake layer.

Prepare the agar-agar with sugar according to its package, stir in the drained fruit cocktail, and pour it over the custard layer once the custard has set. Chill until the agar-agar layer is firm before slicing.
